Sports.title: Cherki and Haaland double up in Manchester City cruise at Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
All who attend the Rayan Cherki show know the ticket comes with a guarantee of entertainment. Enzo Maresca, a manager famed for his obsessive positional control, does not need to put limits on the Manchester City wizard. Cherki has to feel free and he was at his creative best against Crystal Palace, who were in this game before City’s creative heartbeat took it away from them in the second half.

It has been a fine start to the former Lyon player’s second year in England. Cherki was inspired against Bournemouth last week, coming off the bench to spark City’s fightback from 1-0 down with two assists, and this was better. The Frenchman scored twice and the first, a little prod with the outside of his left foot after a mazy run, left you wondering if you have seen something like it before.

Palace, stuck on zero points despite fleeting signs of encouragement in Pierre Sage’s first two outings, had no answer to Cherki’s magic. He is an irrepressible talent and a deep thinker. Listening to the post-match plaudits, Cherki smiled, shrugged and said his performance in the first half was “so shit”. Maresca, though, had a different view.

“His performance for me was very good, not because of the two goals, but the way he worked off the ball,” City’s manager said. “He has to press. His game was complete. He loves football. We know how good he is. We know the quality he has.”

Cherki was not alone in starring for City. Phil Foden impressed and Erling Haaland, who is up and running for the season, grabbed an emphatic double in a performance strong enough to make Maresca think his post-Pep team have moved on from their Community Shield debacle. “We struggled the first five, 10 minutes, because we were pressing in the wrong way,” the Italian said. “After that we were in control.”

A challenge for Maresca is working with an incomplete midfield after the exits of Rodri and Bernardo Silva. Ayyoub Bouaddi has arrived from Lille, £86m an eye-catching fee for an 18-year-old after his exploits for Morocco at the World Cup, but there is room for one more. Enzo Fernández, desperate to leave Chelsea, is the top target before Tuesday’s deadline.

Not that anyone is going to argue that City are short on midfield options. Maresca, ever the tinkerer, shuffled the pack again. The experiment with Marc Guéhi in the engine room was discontinued, allowing him to slot into central defence against his old side. The £116m Elliot Anderson was the sole pivot, Nico O’Reilly pushed high in a 4-1-4-1 system and Josko Gvardiol inverted from left-back, much like Marc Cucurella in Maresca’s Chelsea side.

There are subtle tweaks to the Guardiola template, though some things never change. City led through a familiar source in the 17th minute, Antoine Semenyo crossing from the left and Haaland finding space to loop a clever header over Dean Henderson.

View image in fullscreen Erling Haaland wraps up victory with the fourth goal. Photograph: Richard Heathcote/Getty Images

The defending was poor from Palace, who have had an uncertain summer. They were arranged in familiar fashion, Sage sticking with Oliver Glasner’s 3-4-2-1, but some key faces have gone and others were missing.

Jørgen Strand Larsen led the line in the absence of the unsettled Jean-Philippe Mateta, who may be out for four weeks. Ismaïla Sarr, keen to join Galatasaray, was unavailable and Daniel Muñoz was on the bench amid suggestions of interest from Nottingham Forest. Frailties were inevitable. The defence has lost Maxence Lacroix, sold to Chelsea. Anderson, Semenyo and Foden had chances before half-time. “You saw how we want to play until the 65th minute,” Sage said. “We trust in our process.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Sage likes to play on the front foot. Adam Wharton, subject of a failed enquiry from City recently, swept a ball through for Eddie Nketiah to test Gianluigi Donnarumma in the second minute. Daichi Kamada went close and Tyrick Mitchell fluffed a header after more enterprising play from Wharton.

Palace lacked incision, Nketiah missing again early in the second half. City pressed, O’Reilly and Foden hustling Kamada. Foden advanced and Cherki took over. The Frenchman danced in from the left, danger rising as he wriggled into the area. A host of Palace defenders were thrown off balance, unable to live with Cherki’s footwork and close control. Expect the unexpected. Cherki floated past Jaydee Canvot and held off Chris Richards. For a moment the ball seemed stuck under his feet but he used Takehiro Tomiyasu as a shield and unveiled a finish that was less poke and more dab, Henderson rooted to the spot as the ball rolled tantalisingly over the line.

Palace quickly grabbed a lifeline, Yéremy Pino’s free-kick hitting the woodwork and bouncing in off Donarumma for an own goal, but Cherki was in his element. He scored again in the 59th minute, a fierce shot from 20 yards deceiving Henderson after flicking off Richards.

City sent Bouaddi on for his debut, Anderson withdrawn. They wanted more. Foden, catching the eye in front of Thomas Tuchel, released Haaland. The Norwegian, who has scored in all six of his league games against Palace, was never going to miss.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola tells Liverpool’s forwards to ‘exhaust themselves’
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has said it is more important for Liverpool’s forwards to exhaust themselves than perform for 90 minutes as he prepares to make an “emotional” Premier League bow at Anfield.

The Liverpool head coach hopes his attacking options will be improved by the arrival of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain and another winger before Tuesday’s deadline, with only Victor Muñoz added to his front line so far. The Basque coach has outlined the demands he will put on his forwards as they adapt to a new era at Liverpool.

Iraola said: “For me, wingers, forwards, I always tell them that they don’t need to give us 90 minutes. I tell them it is good news when they are exhausted because then we have taken everything from you and someone else will come in.

“We have the situation now with Jérémy [Jacquet], who hasn’t had a proper pre-season but he is close to getting there. But normally defenders can last 90 minutes easier. For offensive players, it’s not mandatory that you play the whole game. Once you are done, we can change you. I think it’s the best way, and they all have to understand it like this.”

Iraola said Muñoz was “ready to start games” having missed the opening weeks of pre-season as he recuperated from Spain’s victorious World Cup campaign. The 23-year-old impressed from the bench at Newcastle last weekend and was signed for £34.5m from Osasuna on Iraola’s recommendation.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“I had never coached against Victor because he made his debut in La Liga when I was already here in the Premier League but I had very good references of him,” Iraola said. “The club put his name [to me] and we started to analyse his game. We all liked what he gives us. It’s early for him in terms of him not being able to speak the language, and he needs to get a better relationship with teammates, but I like his attitude. He works very hard. He is ready to play right side, left side, and he impacted the game the other day. The subs all played very well.”

Iraola’s wife and two young children will be at Anfield on Saturday – as will the club’s new vice-chair, Amit Bhatia – to witness his first competitive home game, against Nottingham Forest.

“My wife never normally comes to my games,” he said. “But now she is starting to go because my kids want to go. The kids are starting to understand football a little bit and they will sometimes go. Not all the time, but they will be there for the first game because the timing is very good.

“I think there will be an emotional part that is going to be probably only for me. I know it’s my first game but I will not be trying to think too much about those things. Probably when the game finishes, and if it finishes well, then I will be more thinking of myself.”

Sports.title: Premier League news: David Moyes unsettled by Manchester City’s interest in Iliman Ndiaye
Sports.content:
1. City’s Ndiaye bid unsettles Moyes David Moyes has responded to Manchester City’s interest in Iliman Ndiaye by insisting Everton do not have enough time to reinvest money raised through player sales before the transfer deadline. The Everton manager is determined to add to his squad before Tuesday’s deadline, not lose one of his better players such as Ndiaye, with the club still attempting to end their lengthy search for a new right-back. In contrast to the Everton chief executive, Angus Kinnear, who recently claimed the club were planning to challenge for Europe this season, Moyes insisted the squad needs “a lot of work” before it can achieve that target. City have yet to bid for Ndiaye, who has three years remaining on his Everton contract but declined several offers of an extension last season as they did not include a release clause for a Champions League club. “I think it would be very difficult to get it reinvested if anything came in, we are getting into a really late period now,” said Moyes, speaking of player sales in general. On Ndiaye, he added: “I’m certainly not encouraging a bid. I’m not encouraging that in a million years. I don’t know if it would be too tight for time. Deals and contracts are taking much longer now. There seems to be a lot more involved.” Everton remain interested in City’s Jack Grealish, who spent last season on loan at Hill Dickinson Stadium, but a right-back and centre-forward are more of a priority. Moyes added: “I’m saying there’s not much time but I’ll still try to see what we can do. I think we need to do much more if possible. We’re 100% trying to get a right-back and we will try and do that right up until the end of the window.” Everton’s positive start has been tainted by tensions created by Kinnear’s claims that The Friedkin Group, the club’s owners, viewed last season as “a failure” by missing out on European football and that Europe is achievable this term despite only modest investment in Moyes’s team. In response to the latter claim, Moyes said: “There would be a lot of work to do to put us in that category, but nobody put us in that category last year and for most of the season we ran close. You never know. We have started the season well and players have started the games good so that gives me hope that it could be a possibility.” Andy Hunter

2. Milan fixture a riposte to Magpies, says Le Bris Régis Le Bris has said Sunderland’s forthcoming trip to Milan in the Europa League is “a symbol” of the club’s upward trajectory. For many years Newcastle fans have taunted their local rivals with chants of “You’ll never see a Mackem in Milan” and, after arriving from Brittany two years ago, Le Bris swiftly learned that St James’ Park regulars regarded themselves as distinctly superior to Sunderland supporters. Now, though, the tables have turned and Le Bris is enjoying the moment. Sunderland’s manager agreed that it seemed somehow appropriate that the first fixture involving his team to be drawn in Monaco on Friday featured a trip to San Siro. “To get back in Europe with this fixture, it’s a symbol,” said Le Bris, whose side finished seventh in the Premier League last season after beating Newcastle home and away. “It’s iconic. Milan is a massive club and it’s a massive story. “I’m aware of it [the Newcastle fans’ Milan jibes], but I want to speak more about us. We are proud to be in Sunderland and our fans deserve to be in this position. It’s [going to be] a huge experience and we are very proud to be part of it but we want to be efficient. We want to be competitive in the Europa League.” As Sunderland fans began ordering T-shirts and sweatshirts emblazoned with the message “Mackem in Milan” to wear in northern Italy, Le Bris seemed delighted that three players, goalkeeper Robin Roefs, winger Romaine Mundle and the forward Wilson Isidor have signed new long-term contracts at the Stadium of Light. Newcastle fans in Milan in 2023. One of the banners shown says: ‘Have you ever seen a Mackem in Milan?’ Photograph: PA Wire/PA “They see their future in Sunderland because they trust the club and like the environment and they trust the ambition of the club,” said a manager whose side will also face AZ, Dinamo Zagreb, Levski Sofia and Jagiellonia at the Stadium of Light and Anderlecht, Lech Poznan and Torreense away in the Europa League. Le Bris, whose team are at home to Fulham on Sunday, declined to comment on Sunderland’s attempt to sign Jack Grealish on loan from Manchester City but it is believed the former England winger is now most likely to rejoin Everton. Sunderland, meanwhile, remain in the hunt for a right winger and a striker this summer. “I trust the recruitment staff,” said Le Bris. “We are well aligned about the targets we need to make the team better and I still think that we will succeed in the transfer market.” Louise Taylor

3. Gonzalez ‘a smart player with huge potential’ Matthias Jaissle is convinced new arrival Nico González will not take long to hit the ground running after his big-money arrival from Manchester City. The Spaniard could make his Newcastle debut on Saturday at Tottenham after a move from City that could rise to £52m this week, with the head coach excited by the 24-year-old’s ceiling. “He trained with us and he looks sharp,” Jaissle said. “It will take time [to adapt] and I can not tell you how long it takes but he’s a smart player, he has huge potential and already brings so much quality in the squad. He will adapt fast into our way of playing and then we can enjoy.” View image in fullscreen Nico González is presented to the Newcastle fans at St James’ Park: ‘He will adapt fast into our way of playing,’ says Matthias Jaissle. Photograph: Serena Taylor/Newcastle United/Getty Images Jaissle is hopeful that Gonzalez will not be the last player through the door at St James’ Park in this summer’s window, with the Belgium wideman Matias Fernandez-Pardo tipped to move to Tyneside from Lille. “It’s the first message of the morning – to push,” Jaissle said. “The management and Ross [Wilson], the sporting director, they’re doing an amazing job, trying everything. “We want to be smart, we don’t want to act in panic, so I’m really optimistic things will happen.” PA Media

4. Glasner wants to bolster squad after Delap deal Oliver Glasner expects more signings at Nottingham Forest after the arrival of the striker Liam Delap. The 23-year-old joined from Chelsea for a club-record £45m fee on Thursday, and Glasner plans to make further additions before Tuesday’s transfer deadline. Glasner would not comment on a reported £22m Forest offer for his former Crystal Palace wing-back Daniel Muñoz, but the Austrian did admit prospective deals were close to completion. “I think we will add two players,” Glasner said before Saturday’s trip to Liverpool and on the back of home league and Carabao Cup defeats by Leeds. “One we have added, that means we will have at least one more signing. Close deals, quite close to be done, but now from today our focus is on the Liverpool match. That is the most important thing in the next 30 hours and then we have three more days to get the deals over the line.” View image in fullscreen Liam Delap is looking to reignite his career at the City Ground after being frozen out at Chelsea. Photograph: Ritchie Sumpter/Nottingham Forest FC/Getty Images Delap left Chelsea after scoring only two goals in all competitions following his move from Ipswich last summer, and was made to train away from the first-team squad by new Blues manager Xabi Alonso. Glasner said: “It is clear you have to look for a club where you have better chances to get minutes and reignite your career, and that is why we think we are the right club for him.” PA Media

5. O’Neil not finished in transfer market Gary O’Neil has insisted Ipswich are not finished in the transfer window after another busy week at the Premier League newcomers. Argentina international and World Cup winner Exequiel Palacios arrived at Portman Road on Thursday in the latest big-money move secured by the Suffolk club. Talks remain ongoing with the Aston Vila forward Tammy Abraham, who is yet to make a decision on whether to join on a season-long loan, it is understood, but O’Neil is hopeful more can occur in the coming days. Before Sunday’s trip to Manchester United, O’Neil told a press conference: “No, nothing to report on that [Abraham move]. We’re hopefully not finished. We’re still trying to do some business. As to who that is or what positions that will be in, there’s no update from me. “We’re still working hard to try and improve the group, but my focus now is firmly on the game at the weekend and making sure that we’re fully prepared for what is going to be an incredibly tough test.” Ipswich could have Florentino Luís involved at Old Trafford and Palacios is set to make his debut. Azor Matusiwa and Jack Taylor remain sidelined. PA Media

Sports.title: Cartoon alpaca Cole Palmer is a unicorn in this world inventing moments of pure pleasure | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
This week Central Cee launched his new Premier League song, called The Team. It owes its existence to a youth-centred, fist-bumping corporate tie-in with Coca-Cola, the press release for which appears to have involved a man in golf-casual clothing frowning at his computer screen for half an hour before typing “cool urban street words, what are?” into the AI search box, then nipping off for a quick brain-bowl strategy lunch with Roger from the Bluesky Synergy hub.

The song is really good, because Central Cee is really good. He’s super-smart with words, funny and snappy, but also surprisingly tender and raw.

And yes, this is an oh-no-dad’s-talking-about-rap moment. You can just scroll down if you like. The whole thing moves on to Cole Palmer very quickly, why he’s both the best English footballer and very easy to love currently, for various reasons.

Central Cee is a significant figure, perhaps the biggest British recording artist right now. He’s also oddly raw and fearless in the things he says, in a way that feels distinct from the standard, mannered modern person, and which has got him into trouble at least once.

A few years back there was a furore when Central Cee decided to speak out against sexual prejudice. This sounds as if it should just be fine. Except, Central Cee’s call for tolerance was expressed via a lyric in the song Doja. And that lyric was: “How can I be homophobic? My bitch is gay.”

Hmm. Problems there. What Central Cee is saying here, what Central Cee has done while appearing to express a progressive sensibility, is to introduce an entirely new tier of … Basically what he’s saying is: how can I be homophobic? I’m far too busy being sexist.

This caused understandable offence. The b-word is demeaning and cheap, whatever your intentions. Don’t say it. Find better words. To his credit, Central Cee was very good at explaining and apologising, open to other views, while also seeming genuinely non-judgmental of other people regardless of difference or identity, with the exception, of course, of wastemen, mugs and snitches.

He seems to have been forgiven now. More than that, he’s startlingly successful, the most streamed British rap artist of all time. Young people respond to him hungrily. He seems adaptive, fitted to the modern world. In the Coke video he looks blankly into the lens, gives you everything and nothing, risky but also weirdly fearless.

What does this have to do with Cole Palmer, and the surge of heartfelt Palmer-love across all platforms this week after his brilliant performance against Fulham on Monday?

First, Palmer is good friends with Central Cee. He even turned up at the launch of the Coke song just before Chelsea’s Premier League opener. And Palmer really was sensational at Craven Cottage, twirling about between the defensive lines, all perfect touch and interesting angles.

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer was sensational for Chelsea against Fulham at Craven Cottage. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

The reaction was significant too. Everyone went wild for this. In particular passionate football men of a certain age went wild. This boy is gold, this boy gets people off their seats, the man in the TalkSport video chair growled, speaking from the gut and the spleen, coming off less like a piece of football analysis, more like a man offering a brave, husky funeral elegy for a very loyal family dog.

This passion does have an edge to it. It is a mark of how hungry we are for something different, a counterpoint to the dominance of systems football, that despite being entirely academy-coded Palmer still seems to be a unicorn in this world.

For the middle-aged proper football man he can look like a flicker of the pre-digital memory, football in the time of maverick authenticity, an age of mud, of landlines, of not wearing a seat belt, of smoking in pubs, of the casually discarded woodland porn mag, of Barry Davies shouting: “Oh, it’s magnificent and can’t they just taste it” while mods throw darts at each other in the background, because old fun is the best fun.

This is, of course, both deluded and incorrect, because football encourages such feelings and because many middle-aged men are already both of these things. But Palmer is genuinely unusual in the modern game. He turns up in strange spaces, finds gullies and currents in between those static pegs.

Right now he is perhaps the only truly creative English player out there, in the sense of inventing the game in front of him, dishing up in those moments the pure pleasure of a story being told in real time.

He even looks a little unusual in an era of hyper‑athletes. Palmer is light and mobile. He can turn with balletic grace. But he also has that gangly, mischievous physicality, like a very clever cartoon alpaca has worked out how to put on a royal blue football kit and run around occasionally doing amusing celebrations.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

From here Palmer will benefit from having a very good club manager who gets his position. At Bayer Leverkusen Xabi Alonso designed an entire team around getting the best out of Florian Wirtz, the “free electron” in the structure.

Beyond this, Palmer is clearly the player the national team should have been configured around after Euro 2024. It made some logical sense not to pick him for the World Cup, because merit and fitness are also important. But Thomas Tuchel simply has to play Palmer, Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane together now, even if you have to pack the team with cement sacks and tins of beans to make it work, because this is just incredibly hot, and there is literally no other point in playing these games.

But it isn’t just the football. Palmer is also just weirdly likable. There is a temptation to cast him as a Lego-haired blank, some kind of urban idiot savant, a human being made entirely from white bread, energy drinks and discarded phone cases. But he’s clearly very smart, and also very modern in his own way.

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer’s persona is unbothered, wry and oddly gentle. Photograph: Jacques Feeney/Offside/Getty Images

This is another element of the Palmer persona. He looks unbothered, wry and oddly gentle. But the blankness is a thing, a way of being in the middle of all that glare. Palmer gives you nothing to bite on, no gaps in the armour. He even seems weirdly post-race, or just non-race, some kind of bowl-headed omni-man.

It is both an attitude and a shield of sorts. There’s a thing young people do on the internet, known as Nonchalance. This is all about projecting indifference and impassive facial expressions, appearing comically unbothered while chaotic things happen around you. In the picture with Central Cee at the Coke thing they’re both doing it, staring blankly into the camera open but also closed.

Palmer seems to do this naturally. He will sit with his legs crossed while a group of angry men have an on-pitch brawl nearby. He will have the sense of raw dramatic irony to look genuinely amused on the live TV feed as the referee stands right in the middle of the Chelsea huddle, one of the most comically weird sub-moments of the modern age.

There is a theory nonchalance is a political attitude, a response by the post-Gen-Z demographic to the challenge of making the world you find less incoherent, less intrusive on your space, a blank against the constant wall of noise, dogma and ideological boilerplate hurled your way.

Even the way Palmer plays has a kind of shrug about it, an existential creativity, making up your own patterns, making the world small, you-sized, following the lines in front of you.

One of the best bits of Monday night’s game was his interview after. Sky’s reporter Emma Saunders asked Palmer: “How ready are you for this season?” His response was: “Did you not watch the game?” – which from some old‑school, spam-faced football man might have sounded a bit weird, a bit off on power dynamic, a bit man-woman.

But it really wasn’t that at all. Palmer was already laughing. Saunders laughed back. And it was just a nice moment, banter-stuff, mate-chat, playing the game in front of you. English football has such an interesting figure here, not just a brilliant footballer, but a distinct presence, a way of existing in the middle of all that heat. Let’s try not to break him this time.

Sports.title: De Zerbi wants one more signing for Tottenham before transfer deadline
Sports.content:
Roberto De Zerbi is keen to add one more signing to his Tottenham squad and has said outgoing deals are also possible before Tuesday night’s transfer deadline.

De Zerbi had dinner on Thursday night with Spurs’ owners and key executives and they discussed a final push to a window that has already exceeded his expectations. The manager welcomed Omar Marmoush to the club on Thursday from Manchester City and is preparing to involve him in Saturday’s home game against Newcastle. Spurs have also been linked with a move for Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo.

“I didn’t expect a market like we have done,” De Zerbi said. “I think we can do one player more and in one specific position. Yesterday we went for dinner with the owner, with Vinai [Venkatesham, the chief executive], with Johan [Lange, the sporting director] and with Enrico [Venturelli, De Zerbi’s assistant]. We spoke about this.

“It can be possible out or in. The transfer market is crazy and we have to be able to find the new players. If some players go out, leave, or to make another player [come] in … I don’t know. We are very happy with the market we have done until now. It has been more than my expectation at the beginning.”

De Zerbi is open to trimming his squad and mentioned midfielder Pape Sarr as one possible departure. “We have to see in the last day of the market what can happen with him,” he said. “I’ve been very clear with every player. If you speak clearly at the beginning you can’t expect a surprise. The players who want to leave, they left. Maybe we have some players who want to leave and they are waiting for the offer. We are waiting for the offer. To stay here, they have to feel proud and happy.

“If you want to leave and you have not found the offer, it’s your problem, not my problem. I give respect, I kiss you, I hug you, but at the end [they] have to stay calm inside the dressing room. And not to speak too much because the rules have been clear.”

De Zerbi said Mohammed Kudus, who has been out since January with a thigh injury, could return to the bench against Newcastle. He added that Micky van de Ven was “right to play” – in other words to start. He will make a decision on whether to start Pedro Porro and Sávio or use them as substitutes. “Marmoush is available to play, maybe also [at] the beginning of the game,” he said.

De Zerbi considered his established, senior options for the front line, excluding No 10s – Kudus, Sávio, Marmoush, Dominic Solanke, Richarlison, Mathys Tel and Wilson Odobert.

“Odobert is injured for a long time [after ACL surgery],” he said. “Before February, March, he is not available. And then maybe one of these players can leave before the end of the window. I think we are not too many players [in this department.]”

De Zerbi made clear he wanted to include Dejan Kulusevski in the squad he submits to the Premier League after the closure of the transfer window. The attacking midfielder last played on 11 May 2025. Spurs are putting no timeframe on his return from a knee problem.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I hope and I will be very, very happy to see Kulusevski inside of the list and I want to put Kulusevski inside because he is working very well and he’s a different player,” De Zerbi said. “Also Xavi Simons … before March, April, he’s not ready [after ACL surgery]. Kulusevski feels good, he’s improving day by day. He deserves it because he suffered too much for his age. I’m not speaking of him as a player but as a human.”

De Zerbi said he had paid for the meal with the club’s top brass at an Italian restaurant and he was effusive in his praise of how they have driven an expensive reboot of the squad. Spurs have spent £304.5m this summer – a figure that does include the £50m purchase obligation on Marmoush, which is due next summer. He has joined on an initial loan.

“Really, it’s the first time [in my career] that I didn’t push to complete the squad,” De Zerbi said. “They pushed to build [with] the top players. Johan Lange was brilliant in terms of ideas to make solutions. Also, Vinai. I remember when we closed the Sandro Tonali deal, Vinai made a video call to me when I was on holiday and he had a big smile.”

Sports.title: Aston Villa close on Jackson and Mbaye as Emery clears air with departing Watkins
Sports.content:
Unai Emery said Aston Villa were embarking on a “new chapter” as he prepared to welcome Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson and Paris Saint-Germain’s Ibrahim Mbaye in a near £100m remake of his forward line.

Jackson, for whom Villa have paid an initial £47.5m, is in line to make his debut at home to Arsenal on Monday and the club are finalising a move for Mbaye, who will also cost about £47m. They needed to reshape up front after accepting a £50m bid from Al-Hilal for Ollie Watkins and are bringing in further funds by selling Emiliano Martínez to Chelsea for £7.5m.

Jackson and Mbaye have been longstanding targets for the Villa manager. The 18-year-old winger Mbaye, a Senegal teammate of Jackson, was one of the preferred options to strengthen a key position. He played 24 Ligue 1 games for PSG last season, 10 from the start. In recent days, Villa pushed to sign Rafael Leão from Milan but the Portuguese winger is poised to join Galatasaray, whom Villa will visit in the Champions League.

Jackson was Emery’s No 1 target to replace Watkins, who declined the offer of a new contract in favour of a £50m move to the Saudi Pro League club Al-Hilal. Both deals are yet to be formally confirmed. The one for Jackson could rise to a club-record £65m with add-ons.

Emery said Watkins’s departure reduced him to tears and he revealed the England striker apologised to him and his teammates for refusing to play in the 4-0 defeat at Brighton last weekend, leaving Villa without a recognised striker.

“I can tell you his commitment and his behaviour was fantastic always,” Emery said. “He told us after the match he was sorry and he told us that he made a mistake, that he was wrong. We accepted it, the players as well, because he always had very good behaviour and commitment with the club, with us and with me.

“For me, he is a fantastic guy, an even more fantastic a guy than a player. I told him bye with a huge hug and a small tear but now it’s a new chapter here with Nicolas Jackson. A new chapter, we replace him and of course all the best to Watkins in Saudi. With Nicolas Jackson replacing him, we are of course happy.”

Emery dismissed the idea that the manner of Watkins’s departure could tarnish his standing among supporters. Watkins is Villa’s record goalscorer in the Premier League era, with 91 goals across 221 league appearances. “The four years working with him have been a high-level relationship with him as a professional,” Emery added. “Last week I was a little bit disappointed. I was disappointed, but we spoke about it, and now clear. One mistake is not closing all the good things he did here. For the supporters as well. He is class, and I think it’s a legacy here.”

View image in fullscreen Maxim De Cuyper makes it 2-0 to Brighton on a bad day for Aston Villa. Photograph: James Marsh/Shutterstock

Emery said the £50m fees generated for Watkins, who will be 31 in December, and Konsa, who turns 29 in October, were “crazy” given their ages. “We don’t want to be a club to sell players, but the responsibility is to accept it … because for the club it is a good deal. It does not change our objectives.”

Emery acknowledged his side must perform much better against Arsenal than did against Brighton to avoid a second successive defeat. Leon Goretzka, who signed from Bayern Munich on Thursday, could make his debut against the champions, while Zion Suzuki could also feature for the first time after his £30m move from Parma, replacing Martínez.

“Maybe we are not performing like we were performing but the objective is to get to the same way we did, the same performances we had,” said the Villa manager. “We will need time. Last year we showed we needed time. On Monday we will see, [whether] we will need more time or if some players are progressing quickly.”

It promises to be a busy end to the window for Chelsea who, as well as closing in on Martínez, have explored a move for the Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara while they wait for Manchester City to submit their first official offer for Enzo Fernández.

City are yet to make contact with Chelsea over a deal for Fernández, who is desperate to leave before Tuesday night’s deadline. Chelsea are considering their next move and have Camara on a shortlist that also includes Bournemouth’s Alex Scott and Crystal Palace’s Adam Wharton. The Senegal international is not seen as a like-for-like replacement for Fernández but would strengthen Xabi Alonso’s midfield options if the Argentina international joins City.

Chelsea are aware of Bournemouth’s determination not to sell Scott and have received similar messages from Palace regarding Wharton, while Arsenal are understood to have knocked back an inquiry for Martín Zubimendi.

Although there have been suggestions that a deal for Fernández will be close to £106.7m, he will only be allowed to leave if Chelsea’s terms are met. Sources have warned City may have to pay more than the west London club’s initial £120m asking price for the 25-year-old.

Sports.title: Women’s Super League 2026-27 preview No 8: Everton
Sports.content:
Guardian writers’ predicted position: 10th (NB: this is not necessarily Tom Garry’s prediction but the average of our writers’ tips)

Last season’s position: 8th

Prospects

With a new manager in charge, the new season brings some fresh optimism for Everton. But nobody associated with the club will be getting carried away. Last season concluded with a respectable eighth-place finish and anything similar again would be considered a solid campaign for a team operating on a relatively small budget. The latest set of financial accounts showed Everton’s wage bill to be five times smaller than Chelsea’s, illustrating the financial gulf between the Merseysiders and those challenging at the top of the Women’s Super League.

There have been positive elements to Everton’s transfer business this summer, not least the arrivals of Jutta Rantala, Noémie Mouchon and Hannah Cain from relegated Leicester City, as well as turning the Slovenia midfielder Zara Kramzar’s loan move from Roma into a permanent deal. Last season’s loan move for Hannah Blundell from Manchester United has also been converted into a permanent transfer, which was revealed in unusual circumstances, with the 32-year-old emerging from a make-shift ‘coffin’ during an amusing walkout at May’s World Sevens Football event in London.

Scott Phelan’s team have a fairly kind start to the season given they begin with back-to-back matches against newly-promoted sides in Crystal Palace and Charlton Athletic. Their second home league fixture is against the other promoted side, Birmingham City. In between there are meetings with the sides that finished 10th and 11th last season, in West Ham and neighbours Liverpool. Everton do not face any of last season’s top three teams until November. They will, therefore, be keen to make a fast start and get plenty of points onboard before a tougher-looking run of games either side of the winter break.

Off-field picture

Everton’s women’s team was sold to the men’s parent company, Roundhouse Capital Holdings, last year in a move that was understood to be largely aimed at helping ensure the men’s team’s compliance with the Premier League’s profitability and sustainability rules (PSR). The women’s team train at the Finch Farm complex in Halewood, which they share with the men. It is one of the better-equipped facilities enjoyed by a WSL side.

The manager

Phelan was formally appointed in June after a four-month spell in interim charge, taking over from the sacked Brian Sørensen. This is the 38-year-old former Everton youth midfielder’s first senior managerial job, after coaching within the club’s boys’ academy. Phelan deploys a calm, measured approach and has spoken of his “unbelievable pride” at being given this job.

Star signing

There is a lot of excitement at Everton about Australia forward Holly McNamara, signed from Melbourne City, where she won back-to-back Golden Boot awards in the A-League, on a free transfer. If the 23-year-old can replicate her goalscoring form in the northern hemisphere, Everton could well have a strong season and, with McNamara alongside Cain and Mouchon, the Merseyside club have a completely new-look attack. The England youth centre-back Hannah Silcock has also been snapped up from Liverpool, which looks like a very astute piece of business.

View image in fullscreen Holly McNamara won back-to-back Golden Boots during her time at Melbourne City and has been handed the No 9 shirt at Everton. Photograph: Patrick Snow Jr/Everton FC

Stat attack

Despite having the third fewest shots last season, Everton had the third most from Opta-defined fastbreaks (counterattacks). They also scored the joint-most goals from them (four), but that can only carry them so far. Their attack in regular play needs work.

Set for a breakthrough

The England youth defender Naomi Layzell has arrived on loan from Manchester City and Everton and the Lionesses will be hoping it can be a good year for the fit-again 22-year-old. Layzell came to prominence with a goal against Barcelona in the Women’s Champions League two years ago but has since suffered injury misfortune. There is hope at Everton that Layzell can kick on this season and show why she is potentially a future regular for England’s senior side. She has previously been called up to train with Sarina Wiegman’s side.

What they say

“It’s been a tough pre-season in terms of the physical load and things like that, but that’s great preparation for the season. It’s just so important to get everyone on the same page early on. We want to do as well as we can in terms of getting results and being where we want to be in the table” – Everton goalkeeper Courtney Brosnan

Where are they playing their home games?

The women’s team moved to Goodison Park last summer and will continue to play all of their home games there. They made their debut at the Hill Dickinson Stadium last season in a one-off appearance, losing to Manchester United, and while there is no confirmation of when they will next play at the men’s ground, it is understood that is not off the table for the coming campaign.

Sports.title: European football: PSG scramble another draw while Bayern make flying start
Sports.content:
Paris Saint-Germain defender Marquinhos scored deep into stoppage ⁠time to snatch a scarcely deserved 2-2 draw at Lille on Friday as the Ligue 1 champions ⁠continued to struggle ⁠after ​being held by Rennes on the opening weekend.

After the poor 2-2 draw ‌against Rennes, things went from bad to worse for PSG when Lille took the lead in the 21st minute as Icelandic playmaker Hákon Haraldsson latched on to a brilliant reverse pass from Olivier Giroud and curled an unstoppable shot past ‌Matvei Safonov.

Despite all their attacking riches, the Parisians struggled to get shots on target as Lille packed their ​defence and forced the champions to attack from wide areas, and Lille appeared to have secured the three points when Dilane Bakwa scored in the 84th minute.

PSG midfielder Vitinha threw his side ⁠a lifeline in the first minute of stoppage time with ​a superb ​strike curled into the top-left ​corner, and the Portuguese international then crossed for ​Marquinhos to head ‌home the ​equaliser four ​minutes later to complete an improbable comeback.

View image in fullscreen Bayern Munich take the lead as Dayot Upamecano’s effort finds the net against Stuttgart. Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/Reuters

In the Bundesliga Bayern Munich kickstarted their title defence with a resounding 5-1 victory over Stuttgart thanks ⁠to a sparkling second-half display at the Allianz Arena that showed they have lost none of their ⁠potency from last ⁠season.

Goals from ​Dayot Upamecano, Michael Olise, Aleksandar Pavlovic and Luis Díaz capped a superb performance from the hosts during which they also ⁠missed several other opportunities.

It was a mixed night for Stuttgart’s Josha Vagnoman, who scored at both ends having briefly equalised early ⁠in the second half, as Bayern extended their unbeaten run to 15 ‌matches with victory in their first match of the new campaign.

Bayern won the Bundesliga ‌title by 16 points last season, scoring a record 122 goals in the process, ‌and there are signs they could be as dominant again as they created chance after chance against the side who finished fourth last term.

View image in fullscreen Milan supporters display a huge Baresi banner at San Siro before kick-off in the game against Venezia. Photograph: Daniele Mascolo/Reuters

In Serie A Gonçalo Ramos scored with a flashing drive from a tight angle for his first Serie A goal as Milan beat Venezia 2-0 at San Siro. Milan spent €74m to acquire Ramos from PSG and the Portugal forward delivered a goal to treasure on 69 minutes before a late own goal from Redouane Halhal settled the game.

“The most important thing isn’t my goal, it’s the win,” Ramos said. “I should have scored more than one goal tonight.” Milan opened the season with a 2-1 win at Torino making Friday’s encounter their first home game since the death of Franco Baresi and they paid tribute to their former captain before kick-off.

In La Liga, Racing Santander beat Elche 3-2 for their first win since returning to the Spanish top flight, while Alavés beat Villarreal 1-0.

Sports.title: Furious Phil Parkinson shares one-word Wrexham transfer update after Birmingham City defeat
Sports.content:
Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson had just one word to say when asked if he expected his side to be busy in the remainder of the transfer window.

The Welsh side were beaten 2-1 by Birmingham City at home on Friday evening, and Parkinson was asked if he expected to be busy between now and the end of the window.

4 Parkinson was left annoyed by his side's performance against Birmingham Credit: Getty

He simply said, 'possibly' and also wouldn't be drawn on speculation linking them with an ambitious move for Pavel Sulc.

Wrexham are now winless in four at the start of the season with the club expecting to push on this year.

They started the campaign with a 1-0 defeat to Middlesbrough in the Carabao Cup, and there have been two draws against Cardiff City and Watford.

And this evening, they lost to Birmingham, who arrived off the back of a 6-1 defeat to Brentford earlier in the week in the Carabao Cup.

The away side opened the scoring early on as Phil Neumann headed home from Alex Cochrane's corner.

And Neumann scored again in the second half from a recycled throw-in that he headed home unmarked in the box.

Callum Doyle had brought the hosts level, but after Neumann scored again, they didn't look like getting back into the contest.

4 Parkinson was furious with the goals his team conceded Credit: Getty

Speaking in his post-match interview, Parkinson was asked about Sulc joining, and he said: "We get linked with so many players, but at this moment in time, I am just processing the game, but we'll start tomorrow morning and think of where to go."

On the match itself, he said: "Two of the softest goals we've conceded in all my time here.

"I thought we lacked conviction in our play tonight. We got better and equalised, which is why I am so annoyed with the second goal because we started really well.

"We looked like a team that was looking around for someone else to make something happen rather than take responsibility, and that's not us.

"There is a lot of talk around the transfer window and uncertainty. I told the lads at half-time that I wanted them to play with more belief and conviction.

"When we get the hard yards to get a cross in, I want more bodies in there. We had numerous chances to shoot from the edge of the area and didn't. I am hugely disappointed and can't hide away from that.

"In football, you can't feel sorry for yourself, and I felt like we looked like that tonight for some reason because no one is going to help you. We've got to come out hard and fighting at Millwall."

4 Wrexham attempted nine shots in this game, their lowest total in a single match in the Championship this season Credit: Getty

Can only get better

The defending that Parkinson references certainly did leave plenty to be desired.

The first goal was simply an inswinging corner that looped over the top of everyone and dropped onto Neumann's head, and he nodded home.

The second goal was even worse as August Priske launched a long throw into the box.

Kieffer Moore cleared it back to the forward, who volleyed a cross back into the area.

Neumann peeled off his man and glanced home unmarked from close range.

4 Sulc enjoyed a brilliant season for Lyon last year Credit: Getty

Sulc latest

The latest reports suggest that Sulc is a target for Wrexham to become their club-record signing.

The 25-year-old scored 14 goals in all competitions last year for Lyon, and he played in their season opener against Toulouse.

And European football expert Andy Brassell believes that Sulc would become the best player in the Championship if he makes the move.

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT.com, Brassell said: “Lyon paid €7.5million, and he has just been a massive, massive hit. When you look at the sort of players who traditionally thrive in France, he probably shouldn't have been one.

“He’s a forward player, traditionally a second striker. He was sold as an attacking midfielder, but he played as a second striker or false nine. He's done it so well, considering he's built like a sparrow.

“He's had a lot of attention from defenders, but he's smart enough to avoid it.

“He makes great runs. He's technically very adept and considering that he's not the biggest guy, it's actually quite difficult to shove off the ball.

“I think you'd look at someone of that height and build and you'd think, he's not going to do it in the Championship.

“But I think he would. I really think he would. In terms of technical quality, he would be, if not the best player in the division, pretty close because he was one of the better players in Ligue 1 last season.

“They say don't judge people by their friends. Well, firstly, you really should judge people by their friends. Secondly, the way he clicked with Endrick was notable.

“Technically, they're on a level where they can just understand each other. They played really well for a bit until Sulc got injured in the back half of last season.

“That hung over the end of his season and the World Cup and his preseason. Even though he's had his moments in all of those.

“Bear in mind, without Sulc, they wouldn't have got to the World Cup because he is a technically very gifted player in a quite average Czech team, if we're talking about the standards of their best teams. They've had some unreal players down the years."

Sports.title: ‘Created a lot of anger’ – Martin Keown suggests new Premier League rule needs immediate revamp
Sports.content:
‘Created a lot of anger’ – Martin Keown suggests new Premier League rule needs immediate revamp

Martin Keown has called for consistency with the new substitution rule as it caused controversy with Crystal Palace and Manchester City.

During the second half of City's 4-1 victory at Selhurst Park, the hosts looked to bring on Oscar Mingueza for Anan Khalaili.



3 Mingueza was ready to come on for Palace, but needed to wait as Khalaili took too long Credit: Getty

However, Khalaili was deemed to have taken too long to make his way off the pitch, and therefore his replacement had to wait.

The Premier League has introduced a rule to help speed up the game by allowing ten seconds for players to go off at the nearest point.

Should they take longer than this, then the substitute must wait for at least a minute and until a break in play to come on.



It means Palace had to play with ten men for a period of the match before Mingueza was eventually allowed to make his appearance.

Keown questions if new rule needs reviewing

On commentary for talkSPORT, Joe Shennan explained the situation and said: "Well, rules are rules."



"It's intended to stop time-wasting," he added. "No suggestion that's what Palace were doing, they're 3-1 down, but he took too long."

Arsenal legend Keown claimed: "A minute feels like a very long time."

"Does that need looking at?" he later asked. "I'm not sure of that. It felt like five minutes!"



City then made changes of their own towards the end of the half as Ayyoub Bouaddi and Ryan McAidoo were brought on.

Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki replaced them, but the latter took too long to enter the pitch in the eyes of Palace fans.

3 Keown has asked if the new rule needs reviewing after just two weeks Credit: Getty

Many of the home faithful booed and jeered as he made his journey off the pitch in apparent protest to their earlier sanction.



"The irony of this is that Palace fans are saying he's taking too long to go off," Keown explained. "He's milking the applause.

"But the Man City subs are allowed to come on. It's creating a lot of anger here.

Keown added: "That substitution has actually taken a lot longer than the Palace substitution.

"I think what we want is consistency. If you're doing that for one set of players, you must do it for the other."



City go top of the table

After narrowly beating Bournemouth 2-1 last weekend, City were a much more convincing side against Palace.

3 City were on top form in their win at Palace Credit: Getty

Erling Haaland scored his first goal of the season on 17 minutes with an excellent looping header.

Rayan Cherki then scored either side of a Gianluigi Donnarumma own goal to ensure City were cruising en route to victory.



Haaland then added his side's fourth and final goal of the night with six minutes remaining in south London.

City are now top of the Premier League with a 100 per cent record so far this season.

Sports.title: Chelsea starlet’s loan terminated days before transfer window closes amid mocking claims
Sports.content:
Chelsea youngster Kendry Paez has had his loan spell with River Plate terminated, talkSPORT understands.

Paez spent the first half of the 2025/26 season at Strasbourg before moving to Argentina in January on a one-year loan deal.



2 Paez has left River Plate after seven months on loan Credit: Getty

However, the Ecuadorian international played only 461 minutes of football over 14 appearances in all competitions for Los Millonarios.

The 19-year-old is now heading back to Chelsea, whom he joined from Independiente del Valle last summer.

Both he and the Premier League club are discussing his next steps.

Paez addresses mocking claims

Towards the end of his time at River Plate, Paez seemed to irk fans with a post on social media.



River Plate were knocked out of the Copa Sudamerica on penalties in the last 16 by Colombian side Independiente Santa Fe.

According to Radio Gol, a post that appeared to be attributed to Paez was eyed as a dig at the club and his teammates following the defeat.



He was not involved in either leg against Santa Fe as he was part of a group of players training away from the first team.

Paez then posted on his Instagram to publicly deny making the post.

It translated to: "I have seen that a story that I supposedly published after the game is circulating on networks and I wanted to clarify that that publication never left my account.



"I don't usually go out to clarify this kind of thing, but in this case I felt it was important to do it out of respect for River, my colleagues and all the people who accompanied me during this time.

2 Paez, who played at the World Cup, could be set for another loan Credit: Getty

"I would never post something to make fun of a result or a difficult moment of the team."

Paez could feature for Chelsea's newly-named Cobham Next Gen sides this season, or have a third loan spell away from the club.



Chelsea summer business continues

With the September 1 transfer deadline looming, Chelsea are working hard to finalise their incomings and outgoings.

Emiliano Martínez is due to join from Aston Villa in a £7.5million move and sign a two-year deal at Stamford Bridge.

Chelsea are also now in talks with Monaco over a move to sign Lamine Camara, who has been eyed as a potential replacement for the Manchester City-linked Enzo Fernandez.

AS Monaco man Camara is available for between £50m and £60m, with Chelsea hoping to bank double this amount for Fernandez.

Sports.title: Man United issued key transfer ultimatum as Michael Carrick warned of ‘sackable offence’
Sports.content:
Manchester United must stop dallying with Kobbie Mainoo and play him in midfield - or let him leave this summer.

That's the demand made by Adrian Durham on the latest episode of Fiery Fridays, with his talkSPORT colleague Alex Crook also issuing a warning to head coach Michael Carrick over Mainoo's involvement.

4 Mainoo may no longer be a starting midfielder for United Credit: Getty

Mainoo is arguably the best player to have progressed through the United academy in recent years, with the 21-year-old already on 103 senior appearances across all competitions.

He starred during the second half of last season under Carrick as they qualified for the Champions League.

However, Mainoo did not start in their shock 2-0 defeat to Hull City on the opening weekend of the new Premier League season amid an influx of new midfield signings.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans joined earlier in the summer for a combined £85million, with Carlos Baleba the latest arrival at Old Trafford in a move from Brighton that is worth at least £70m.

Mainoo is therefore facing increased competition in midfield at his boyhood club and Durham believes United need to make a decision on his future, or risk affecting his career.

United must stop 'messing around' with Mainoo

"I'm going to start with a quote," he said on Fiery Fridays. "This was from a director of football at a top English club, you may be able to guess which one. This quote is from April this year. It's about a player who went to the World Cup.

"The quote is as follows, 'He is one of the most naturally gifted young footballers in the world'. The director of football who said that? Jason Wilcox. The player he's praising? Kobbie Mainoo.

"Since then, United have signed a clutch of midfielders, spending over £150m. Significantly, they've spent £70m on another Kobbie Mainoo. Carlos Baleba is box to box, high energy, can play defensive midfield as a speciality as well.

"This is pretty much what I'm hearing Kobbie Mainoo is meant to be, if ever we get to see him on the pitch. Interestingly, Andrey Santos fits a very similar description, defensive midfielder or progressive central midfielder.

"Tielemans is described as the link between defence and attack. These are all very similar players. Mainoo is described as box to box or advanced centre mid. I think we'll all appreciate he could be more of an advanced midfielder.

4 United have been told to make a decision on his future amid the end of the window Credit: Getty

"Now, to be fair to Wilcox, he has said they're building a squad to cope with all competitions. He said that out loud. United will possibly play 20, 25 more games this season than the pathetic amount of 40 that they did last season because they were so bad… so that's one reason for so many similar midfielders.

"Mason Mount still lurking in the vicinity as well, by the way. Where does it leave Mainoo? Could it leave him challenging for the no. 10 role with Bruno Fernandes? And if he is, will he ever play football for United again?

"Wilcox describing him as one of the most naturally gifted footballers in the world, high praise. And he signed a contract at that time, keeping him at Old Trafford till 2031.

"Since then, he's gone to the World Cup only because (Thomas) Tuchel refused to take Cole Palmer or Phil Foden. Didn't even get on the pitch at the World Cup, with all sorts of stories floating around as to why he didn't get on the pitch, and none of them good as far as Kobbie Mainoo is concerned.

"And he was left out of the starting lineup for United's first Premier League game of the season. That's apparently one of the best midfielders United have ever had, leaving out a midfielder who the director of football seems to love.

"So, what's going on? United aren't spending big on midfielders just to leave them out of the team. Do they really rate Mainoo? Is he actually any good?

4 Carrick brought Mainoo on in the second half of their defeat at Hull Credit: Getty

"Four years ago, Kobbie Mainoo won the Youth Cup with United. The star of that team was Alejandro Garnacho... we all know what's happened to him. Is Mainoo going the same way?

"And so, here's my Fiery Fridays hot take. It's a message to Man United, really. You're messing with a player's career, telling him he's brilliant, then spending big on other midfielders and leaving him out. Stop messing Mainoo around. United should play him or sell him."

Carrick decision would be a 'sackable offence'

Against Hull, Carrick opted for a midfield pairing of Tielemans and Santos, who struggled throughout and were both substituted.

They return to Old Trafford on Sunday evening to host Ipswich Town and Crook believes that if Mainoo doesn't start, then Carrick would be worthy of dismissal.

After seemingly agreeing with Durham, he added: "You look at the impact he had in the second half of last season alongside Casemiro. He made Casemiro look like his legs hadn't gone.

"And then Casemiro turned up at the World Cup, played alongside Bruno Guimaraes (for Brazil), and proved to us, actually, his legs have definitely gone, and United were right to get rid of him. So, I think he is harshly treated.

"I think maybe it's because he's come through the academy, didn't cost the club a penny, and therefore it's easier to leave him out than it is a £70m shiny new toy in Carlos Baleba, or £50m shiny new toy in Andrey Santos, or a £35m shiny new toy in Youri Tielemans.

"But make no bones about it, Tielemans and Santos were a car crash at Hull at the weekend and if Michael Carrick picks that same midfield against Ipswich on Sunday, that is a sackable offence, in my opinion.

4 Crook has insisted that Mainoo must start against Ipswich this weekend Credit: Getty

"Kobbie Mainoo has to start this game. Tielemans didn't look fit, didn't look up to speed. So I'd imagine it will be Mainoo in alongside Santos. And this is his opportunity, he knows he's got that pressure coming with Baleba, who's not fit yet because of an ankle injury.

"So he's got an opportunity now to nail down a place in the team, to prove Thomas Tuchel he was wrong, to prove the Portuguese idiot (former boss Ruben Amorim) he was wrong, and to prove Michael Carrick he was wrong for leaving him out of the first game of the season.

"United cannot sell this player because the history of this football club is built on nurturing their own talent. It's built on the Busby Babes and Fergie's fledglings.

"The production line from the academy has run dry. There's a lot of high hopes for JJ Gabriel, who was brilliant in midweek, scored a terrific goal. He's not committed his future yet, and there's a bit of interest from elsewhere.

"They can't afford to let one of their rivals come in and snare him away because by all accounts, he is the real deal. But they've got to build this team around Kobbie Mainoo.

"So I'll make you right, Adrian, I don't think they should sell him. I definitely think they should start him."

Sports.title: Harvey Elliott offered career lifeline by Spanish club once managed by his namesake
Sports.content:
Harvey Elliott offered career lifeline by Spanish club once managed by his namesake

Harvey Elliott could have a career lifeline from an unexpected source before the close of the transfer window.

Reports are suggesting that Valencia are in talks over the versatile midfielder, who looks destined to leave Liverpool before the deadline.

3 Elliott was part of the Aston Villa squad that won the Europa League, but due to a clause in his contract, he barely played Credit: Getty

Transfer journalists Fabrizio Romano and Matteo Moretto are both reporting that the Spanish giants are leading the race for the 23-year-old.

Three other clubs are trying to sign Elliott before the end of the transfer window.

However, Valencia are advancing in talks with Liverpool after agreeing terms with the player.

The former England Under-21 international doesn't appear to be part of Andoni Iraola's plans, having been left out of the squad for Liverpool's opening Premier League game against Newcastle United.

Harvey Elliott transfer to Valencia

Should he join Valencia, he would become just the second English player to represent the LaLiga side - although they were once managed by former Tottenham player Jimmy Elliott in the 1920s.

However, the only other English player to actually play a competitive game for the club is Max Aarons.

The ex-England U21 full-back joined Valencia on loan from Bournemouth in January 2025.

It wasn't the most successful loan spell, given he made just five appearances, but Elliott could follow in his footsteps.

3 Elliott was heavily involved in pre-season, but he played no part at St James' Park Credit: Getty

Last year, Elliott joined Aston Villa on loan near the end of the transfer window.

The deal was a loan with an obligation to buy for £35million.

This would have been triggered if Elliott had appeared a certain number of times.

However, Unai Emery revealed very early on that Elliott wouldn't be playing that much because of the clause.

Villa decided they didn't want to sign Elliott at all, so he spent the majority of last year on the bench.

Across all competitions, he played just ten games for Villa.

3 Elliott is looking to revive his career, and he is still very young Credit: Getty

Iraola not convinced

When asked about why Elliott played no part against Newcastle, his manager had a pretty brutal response.

In his post-match interview, he said: “Harvey is trying and improving every week, but I still prefer other options, about the balance on the bench.

“That’s why James McConnell was in the squad, but it’s now another new week and new chances for everyone. They have to keep that mentality!”

And before hearing about this news, Ally McCoist was on talkSPORT Breakfast this morning.

He urged Elliott to have a sit-down with Iraola about his future.

He said: “He has got to get playing – it doesn’t look like it will be at Liverpool.

“It is a slippery slope, and he has to be very careful. I don’t imagine wage demands will be that high, but he needs to go and play. Whether it is in Europe or with another English club, I don’t know, but the Villa spell was a nightmare.

“He needs to sit down with Iraola and find out if he has a chance or if he is in his plans because he needs to play.

"He is a lovely footballer. Last season was a write-off, and he can’t afford another one like that.”

Sports.title: Liverpool move for Paris Saint-Germain star hijacked by surprise Premier League rivals
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have reached an agreement in principle with Paris Saint-Germain to sign Ibrahim Mbaye, talkSPORT understands.

The 18-year-old is due to join the Premier League club in a €55million (£47m) deal.

2 Mbaye now appears to be heading for Villa Credit: Getty

Mbaye's move to Villa Park will come as a blow to Liverpool, who have long been linked with him this summer.

European football journalist Andy Brassell tipped Mbaye as an ideal alternative for the Reds if they were unable to agree a deal for his PSG teammate Bradley Barcola.

However, it's Villa who appear to have won the race for the highly-rated teenager, who has played 42 times for PSG.

Mbaye will join Alejandro Garnacho, a season-long loan signing from Chelsea, as a new winger option.

talkSPORT understands that Villa are now working on personal terms, and Liverpool only held exploratory talks for the winger.

Villa seal shock deal for Mbaye

In a battle to comply with PSR (Profit and Sustainability Rules) and SCR (squad coast ratio), Villa have had to sell numerous players.

Morgan Rogers was the first big departure in a record £117m transfer to Chelsea, and Ezri Konsa has joined Arsenal for around £50m.

Youri Tielemans also left for Manchester United in a £35m switch, so much of Villa's Europa League-winning side has been dismantled.

However, with just days remaining until the September 1 transfer deadline, Villa are giving one final push to strengthen for the season.

Johan Manzambi became their club-record signing in July as he made a £59.5m move from SC Freiburg.

2 Emery is welcoming new additions before the end of the window Credit: Getty

This is set to be beaten by the arrival of Nicolas Jackson, who is set to sign in a £65m switch from Chelsea.

Mbaye's deal won't be as expensive, but he will arrive at the club as a much-needed addition after a disastrous start to the season.

Villa were well-beaten 4-0 by Brighton and had Joao Gomes sent off in their Premier League opener.

It means they will enter matchweek two of the 26/27 campaign as the side sitting bottom of the table.

Villa host reigning champions Arsenal on bank holiday Monday night, live on talkSPORT.

Jackson will be able to feature against the Gunners, but Mbaye is not set for selection as he awaits the finalisation of his move from PSG.

Sports.title: Top ten most expensive summer transfers so far: Chelsea, Man City and Spurs all confirm £100m deals
Sports.content:
Top ten most expensive summer transfers so far: Chelsea, Man City and Spurs all confirm £100m deals

Premier League clubs have been hard at work splashing the cash this summer, with three clubs already completing nine-figure deals.

The transfer record for a British player has been broken with Chelsea sealing the £117million capture of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.



13 Rogers has joined Chelsea in a blockbuster deal

The 2026 summer window officially opened on June 15, with talkSPORT.com already providing a completed list of every deal.

Due to certain PSR constraints, some initial-loan agreements in previous windows have since become permanent this summer.

The rising inflation in the transfer market also means relegation is no longer a signal for clubs to poach key players on the cheap.



With that in mind, teams have had to open up their chequebooks. Below are the top 10 most expensive arrivals in the Premier League...

=10. Maxence Lacroix (Crystal Palace to Chelsea) - £52m

Chelsea have spent upwards of £330m this summer, including announcing Maxence Lacroix has joined the club.



The French centre-back signed for £52m, matching Jan Paul van Hecke's move from Brighton to Tottenham.

After joining, Lacroix labelled the club as the 'best in the world' and said he matched the desire of manager Alonso.



He has also become the 14th most expensive defender ever in the Premier League following his big-money move.

13 Lacroix has left Crystal Palace to sign for Chelsea in a big-money deal Credit: Getty

=10. Jan Paul van Hecke (Brighton to Tottenham) – £52m

The Netherlands defender's move to Spurs wasn't part of the deal that saw Vuskovic head in the opposite direction.

However, on the balance sheet, Roberto De Zerbi reunited with his former Brighton player for a nominal fee, all things considered.



Tottenham were persistent in their bid to land Van Hecke, with Seagulls CEO Paul Barber revealing on talkSPORT that the Lilywhites had two previous bids rejected.

The Dutchman, who cost Brighton just £1.8m from NAC Breda in 2020, was entering the final year of his contract with Hurzeler's side.

13 De Zerbi has worked with the Dutch defender before on the south coast Credit: AFP

=10. Johan Manzambi (Freiburg to Aston Villa) - £52m

Unai Emery's side have been involved in the biggest transfer of the summer so far, but have also broken their club record on a player.



The West Midlands club snapped up Manzambi for £52m, which surpassed the £50m forked out to land Amadou Onana in 2024.

Newcastle were close to signing the midfielder, having agreed a deal in principle with Freiburg for £51m, before Villa swooped in.

The 20-year-old played against Villa in the Europa League final, while he also scored three goals for Switzerland in the World Cup but is struggling with a knee injury ahead of the new season.

13 Villa broke their transfer record to sign the Switzerland midfielder Credit: Getty Images



9. Jeremy Jacquet (Rennes to Liverpool) – £60m

Liverpool completed the biggest deal of the winter window's deadline day by beating Chelsea to land the France U21 international.

talkSPORT understands that the Reds agreed an initial £55m to sign Jacquet, with a further £5m to be paid in potential add-ons.

A move for the defender eclipsed the £52m fee spent by Manchester City on Jeremy Doku in 2023 to become Rennes' record sale.

However, the 21-year-old spent the second half of last season at his boyhood club, with a move to Anfield only becoming official on July 1.



13 Jacquet inherited Ibrahima Konate's No.5 shirt at Liverpool Credit: Getty

8. Carlos Baleba (Brighton to Manchester United) - £70million

Manchester United secured the signing of Baleba a year after they began their pursuit of the Cameroon international.

The Red Devils landed Baleba in a deal that is worth at least £70million, with a sell-on clause also included.

That is significantly less than what Brighton were demanding last summer, when they valued him at around £115m.



Having experienced a dip in performances after his move to Old Trafford failed to materialise a year ago, Baleba will now be looking to rediscover the form that made him such a hot property.

13 Baleba completed his move to Man United, which has been over a year in the making Credit: Getty

7. Bruno Guimaraes (Newcastle to Arsenal) – £75m

Amid the swathe of departures at Newcastle, former Toon captain Guimaraes as headed to the champions.

The Brazil star has signed a four-year deal in north London and called the move one of the 'toughest decisions' of his life.



The 28-year-old scored 31 goals in 195 appearances for Newcastle, having joined them from Lyon for £40m in 2022.

"I'm at the point of my life, I think I need a challenge like this," Guimaraes said. "I want to win trophies, I want to make history and I think I'm in the right place to do it. I'm so excited to start."

13 Bruno Guimaraes is now an Arsenal star Credit: Getty

=5. Savinho (Manchester City to Tottenham) - £85m

Savinho became Spurs' latest big-money arrival when he finally moved to north London in a deal worth up to £85m.



The 22-year-old had looked set to join the club last summer, only for the transfer broke down, but he is now officially a Tottenham playing, in a move worth an initial £75m with an extra £10m in add-ons.

Having struggled for game time at Man City after his £31m arrival from Troyes, Savinho is looking to rediscover his best form at Spurs.

The Brazilian got off to the perfect at his new club just a day after signing, as he marked his debut with a goal in Tottenham's 5-1 Carabao Cup demolition of Charlton in a hugely exiting cameo.

13 Savinho is already up and running in a Tottenham shirt Credit: Getty



=5. Mateus Fernandes (West Ham to Tottenham) – £85m

Spurs have broken their transfer record twice this summer, the first of which saw Fernandes arrive from their relegated London rivals.

The 22-year-old was one of the standout Premier League midfielders last season, despite West Ham's struggles.

He scored five top-flight goals and registered four assists in 41 appearances but missed out on Portugal's World Cup squad.

However, Troy Deeney told talkSPORT that he questioned whether Fernandes was really the player to 'change the mentality' at Tottenham after his successive relegations, having also failed to beat the drop at Southampton.



13 Spurs beat off competition from Manchester United to secure Fernandes' signature Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

4. Ayyoub Bouaddi (Lille to Manchester City) - £86m

Manchester City made Morocco star Bouaddi the most expensive teenager in Premier League history by some distance.

After impressing at the 2026 World Cup, the 18-year-old joined City from Lille in a deal thought to be worth £86million.

The fee obliterates the previous record fee for a player under the age of 20 in England's top-flight, previously held by Romeo Lavia following his £58m move to Chelsea in 2023.



Big things are expected of Bouaddi, who has earned a strong reputation in French football since bursting onto the scene with Lille as a 16-year-old in 2023

13 Bouaddi became one of the most expensive teenagers in history by joining Manchester City Credit: Getty

3. Sandro Tonali (Newcastle to Tottenham) – £100m

Spurs shattered their transfer record again to poach the Italian from Newcastle less than a week after unveiling Fernandes.

Tonali joined De Zerbi's side in a £100m deal - an initial £92.5m fee with £7.5m in proposed add-ons.



The 26-year-old made 110 appearances across his three seasons with Newcastle after his reported £52m move from AC Milan in July 2023.

But he was accused by talkSPORT Breakfast co-host Gabriel Agbonlahor of joining Tottenham 'for the big bucks'.

13 Tonali is the latest key player to leave St. James' Park after signing for Tottenham Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

2. Elliot Anderson (Nottingham Forest to Manchester City) – £116m

Man City were the first of two clubs to break the transfer record for a British player following their capture of Anderson at the start of July.



The England international sealed his move to the Etihad Stadium from Nottingham Forest for a fixed £116m fee while at the World Cup.

Forest have tried to claim the deal is worth a total of £130m, which would eclipse the Premier League transfer record set by Liverpool's £125m signing of Alexander Isak, but City dispute this.

Anderson featured in all of England's games during their run to third at the World Cup - their best finish at the tournament since 1966.

13 Anderson put in some heroic midfield performances Credit: talKSPORT



1. Morgan Rogers (Aston Villa to Chelsea) - £117m

Anderson's reign as the most expensive British player lasted mere weeks as his England teammate Rogers took the crown.

The 23-year-old was the leading target at Arsenal, but he has now signed a six-year deal, with the option of another 12 months, at their London rivals Chelsea.

"I'm so excited," Rogers said on the move.

"For me, Chelsea are the biggest club in London and a club I've always admired since I was a kid.

13 Rogers made three starts and a further four sub appearances for England at the World Cup Credit: Getty



"I'm really excited about the project with the new manager, the players we've got and where the club is heading. That's why I'm here, and I can't wait to get started.

"The way the club wants to go and how it wants to move forward, it's something I want to be a part of, and I think it was just perfect for me.

"I'm a free spirit, free-flowing footballer. I like to take risks, make things happen, change games. Whatever that may take. Just can't wait to get started."

Head over to talkSPORT BET for all the latest transfer odds ahead of the key moves this summer
