World.title: Black Coffee’s R7.7 million legal WIN over missing supercar
World.content:
DJ Black Coffee, aka Nkosinathi Innocent Maphumulo, is a self-proclaimed petrol head of the highest order. If there’s a high-performance supercar out there, he’s probably owned it.

A quick squiz through his Instagram page reveals his Ferrari 458 Speciale, Porsche 911 Turbo, McLaren GT, Bentley Flying Spur, Maserati MC20 and more …

However, it is the Grammy-award-winning DJ’s fight over a R7.7 million Maserati open-top supercar that is making headlines this week.



It’s been widely reported that Casa Vehicle Holdings, trading as Maserati SA, faces a writ of execution issued on 17 August 2026.

As such, this directs the sheriff to attach and auction the company’s movable goods to recover monies owed to Black Coffee.

BLACK COFFEE’S SUPERCARS

According to reports, the dispute has its roots back in 2022. Black Coffee purchased a Maserati MC20 Coupe for around R7 million.



Two years later, he agreed to trade that car in toward a custom-spec, open-top version, the MC20 Cielo, priced R2 million dearer at roughly R9 million. You must remember that Maserati is a boutique car manufacturer from Italy.

Everything is strictly made to order. And while roughly 1 200 MC20s are built annually, the more exclusive Cielo and MCPura models (pictured below) are built in such few numbers that the brand doesn’t even disclose how many (likely only a few hundred annually).

Nevertheless, delivery of the DJ’s supercar was promised in July 2025. However, a month before, the dealership delivered the bad news that his car had not even started being built, and no firm delivery date could be given.



WHAT HAPPENS NEXT?

Promotional image of the Maserati MCPura Cielo in Italy. Image: File

Black Coffee wanted out of the deal. But before entering into litigation, he did try to settle the matter directly.

Correspondence from Maserati SA allegedly shows the factory had made a ‘special exception’ to move him up in the queue.

It cited the DJ’s global profile.

However, because the company failed to mount a substantive defence, judge Sanet van Aswegen granted summary judgment in favour of Soulistic Music, the DJ’s company.



Maserati must repay the R7 million, plus interest at 10.5% a year from August 2025 until settled, plus legal costs.

At last count, this adds up to R7.7 million. It’s unclear whether Maserati SA intends to appeal the judgement.

But what do you think? Is Black Coffee right to be pursuing legal matters? Or is this an merely an unavoidable incident from the manufacturer? Please share your thoughts in the comments section below …

World.title: Beyond Game Day | Why Are South Africa’s Sports Federations Failing? | 28 August 2026
World.content:
South African Athletes Cannot Keep Carrying Broken Federations

South African athletes are repeatedly asked to produce excellence inside sporting systems that struggle to provide stability, funding and credible leadership.

When those athletes succeed, administrators often share the applause. When performances fall short, however, the competitor becomes the easiest person to blame. The federation’s role in creating the conditions behind that result receives far less scrutiny.

That imbalance matters.

Elite sport requires more than talent and determination. Athletes need reliable coaching, suitable facilities, nutrition, medical care, competitive opportunities and enough financial security to focus on performance. Yet many South African competitors must balance training with ordinary employment while facing opponents whose full-time job is to prepare.

Parents, coaches and private sponsors frequently step into the gaps. Their support keeps careers alive, but it can also conceal the extent of institutional failure. A federation may appear functional because athletes continue winning medals, even when the machinery behind those achievements is barely moving.

Swimming South Africa has become another flashpoint in the wider debate about governance. Questions surrounding its senior leadership arrive alongside longstanding concerns involving other national federations, including Athletics South Africa and the South African Football Association.

SAFA remains the most visible example because football commands enormous public attention and substantial resources. Disputes involving money, leadership, refereeing and the introduction of VAR are not isolated administrative inconveniences. They affect the credibility and development of the entire game.

The problem is also generational. Institutional knowledge is valuable, but experience should not become permanent ownership. Healthy organisations renew themselves. They build succession plans, develop younger administrators and recognise when leadership has stopped serving the institution’s future.

South African rugby offers a useful, though imperfect, comparison. Its structures draw a clearer distinction between elected custodians and professionals appointed to run the sport. From high-performance management to national teams across different levels, the system operates around a broadly shared vision.

That alignment does not eliminate mistakes. It does, however, make sustained success more possible.

The lesson is not that every federation should copy rugby line by line. It is that governance must create the conditions in which athletes can succeed consistently. Leadership should serve the sport, protect its credibility and leave it stronger for the next generation.

South Africa does not lack sporting talent. It lacks enough institutions worthy of that talent.

World.title: Three women nabbed for the alleged illegal sale of abortion pills
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Three women will spend the weekend behind bars after they were arrested for the alleged theft and illegal sale of termination-of-pregnancy medication.

It is alleged that the stolen medication was sold to women waiting in the Choice on Termination of Pregnancy (CTOP) queue at Stretford Community Health Centre in Orange Farm, Johannesburg.

The women attached to the Expanded Public Works Programme were arrested on Thursday and are expected to appear in court on Monday.

The Gauteng Department of Health welcomed the arrest as it detailed the investigations into the incident which happened on 24 August.

READ | IN PICS | Dagga, nyaope and abortion pills found in Gauteng schools

According to the Gauteng Department of Health spokesperson Steve Mabona, the suspects allegedly stole two boxes of Cytotec tablets and 24 loose tablets after breaking a padlock securing a medication cupboard.

Subsequent to investigations, the three women were arrested.

"A sting operation was conducted, which led to the apprehension of one of the suspects, who allegedly sold the stolen medication to clients waiting in the CTOP queue at the facility. “A client who had purchased the tablets assisted investigators by identifying the individual who sold the medication. Further investigations led to the implication of additional accomplices,” Mabona said.

Mabona said the department condemns this incident, adding that such criminal conduct undermines the integrity of the public healthcare system.

READ | IVF error leaves two families facing a life-changing identity crisis

He also cautioned against purchasing termination of pregnancy medication illegally as it has significant health risks.

World.title: From 10 to 38: Cabinet flags municipalities in distress
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - While cabinet is applauding the launch of Phase 3 of the government-business partnership, there are still concerns around stagnant economic growth, fuel shortages and the alarming levels of crime in the country.

Cabinet received a sobering update on the country's local government crisis, with the number of officially distressed municipalities skyrocketing from 10 to 38.

This was confirmed by Minister in the Presidency, Khumbuzo Ntshavheni, during a post-Cabinet briefing on Friday.

“The intervention has been extended from the initial 10 to 38 municipalities and focuses on improving financial viability, governance, service delivery, audit outcomes and institutional capacity," Ntshavheni said.

Noticeably left off the table were two massive national issues.

Officials failed to discuss the turbulent state of the National Student Financial Aid Scheme, as well as the jet fuel shortages facing major airports.

"The jet fuel shortage was not discussed in Cabinet, but the last time that IMC was looking at the fuel shortages, we were assured that there is capacity to make sure that there is sufficient jet fuel. “On the NSFAS, it was not discussed in Cabinet, but the Minister of Higher Education and Training is busy working on mechanisms to make sure that NSFAS is stabilised and that there is continuity and funding."

Cabinet also welcomed the extension of AGOA for the next two years.

World.title: 'The truth, I am confident, will vindicate me' - Sibanyoni
World.content:
PRETORIA - Controversial Mpumalanga taxi boss Joe "Ferrari" Sibanyoni used the last few minutes of his testimony before the Madlanga Commission of Inquiry to defend his reputation.

As he read out the closing remarks of his statement, he began by reiterating that he has spent more than 42 years building what he described as a ‘legitimate life'.

He told the Commission that he intervened to prevent violence in the taxi industry when others chose not to intervene

Sibanyoni took the stand on Friday after he was summoned to alleged criminal syndicates, and their associates even reported the criminal cabal to the Minister of Police.

READ | LIVESTREAM | Joe 'Ferrari' Sibanyoni testifies at Madlanga

As he continued to read the last bit of his statement to the record, Sibanyoni also touched on surviving a 2022 ambush in Centurion.

This is the same failed assassination attempt which Vusimuzi 'Cat' Matlala has allegedly been linked to and is in court for.

“When the National Prosecuting Authority charged the men who tried to kill me, I stood ready to testify against him, and now I sit before the Commission of Inquiry, being asked whether I discussed the hiring of his men. I understand why this Commission must ask difficult questions of everyone in its scope. I do not resent the process; I respect it,” Sibanyoni told the commission.

Despite the allegations surrounding his name, including the alleged extortion and money laundering case, Sibanyoni maintains that he has never been convicted of any crime.

He told the Commission: “My dignity is not negotiable, my cooperation is genuine, and the truth, I am confident, will vindicate me.”

Sibanyoni will be back before the Commission on 21 September.

World.title: IEBC rejects Gachagua's claims, defends 2027 polls preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC dismissed Gachagua's claims of political interference, graft and voter suppression in 2027 polls.

The Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has dismissed allegations of political interference, corruption and voter suppression surrounding preparations for the 2027 General Election, terming the claims false, unsubstantiated and aimed at undermining public confidence in the electoral body.

In a statement issued on Thursday, IEBC Chairperson Erastus Edung Ethekon said the allegations followed statements made by Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua during a press briefing on Wednesday.

The commission specifically rejected claims that politicians had purchased a house for its chairperson to influence him, saying the allegation had changed from an alleged Sh80 million property to one worth Sh200 million.

"The allegations that a house has been purchased for the Chairperson of IEBC by some politicians for purposes of influencing him are unfortunate, unfair and unsubstantiated to date," Ethekon stated.

The commission also challenged Gachagua to provide evidence, including the location of the property, sale and transfer documents, payment receipts and details of the parties involved, and submit them to the Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission for investigation.

The electoral body also dismissed claims of improper staff changes, saying deployment and redeployment of employees was part of its normal administrative functions and was guided by its human resource policies and public service regulations.

"The Commission complies with its Human Resource policies, guidelines and other relevant instruments under the larger public service when engaging employees," the statement read in part.

It further denied allegations of malpractice against the chairperson and vice-chairperson, describing them as fabricated claims intended to damage the reputation of the commissioners and the commission.

Magarini by-election

On the Magarini by-election, IEBC said the poll was conducted in a free, fair and credible manner and was not challenged through an election petition. The commission added that it had successfully conducted several by-elections and was prepared to oversee the 2027 General Election.

At the same time, IEBC also defended its procurement process for election technology and ballot papers, saying all tenders were being conducted in accordance with Chapter 12 of the Constitution and the Public Procurement and Asset Disposal Act, 2015.

"Two key tenders, one for the Integrated Elections Management System, hardware and accessories, and another for ballot papers and other election materials, have temporarily been halted following a request for review filed before the Public Procurement Administrative Review Board," IEBC stated.

According to IEBC, documents for the technology tender were uploaded on its website and the Public Procurement Information Portal on August 11, 2026.

The commission said the technical specifications were generic and performance-based and open to all qualified suppliers. It stressed that the procurement process was still at its initial stages and that no company had been awarded the tender.

Voter register protected

The commission also dismissed claims that voter registration data could be manipulated or shared with external parties, insisting that the Register of Voters remained under its exclusive custody.

"Voter registration involves several stages, including in-person registration, verification of identity, collection of biometric and biographical data, transmission to a central database and automated biometric deduplication," IEBC added.

Flagged records are subjected to data cleaning, validation and adjudication before valid records are incorporated into the register.

The register will subsequently undergo a 30-day biometric verification exercise, followed by an independent audit before it is finalised and certified for use in an election.

IEBC said allegations of bribery, predetermined tender awards and voter suppression were false and potentially harmful to public confidence in the electoral process.

World.title: Ruto hands Sh2.6bn to Mau Forest evictees
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto also announced the lifting pf the caveat that had been placed on land bordering the Mau Forest. [PCS]

President William Ruto has announced the payment of Sh2.6 billion to 13,000 families evicted from the Mau Forest in Narok six years ago, marking what he described as the closure of a long chapter.

Each beneficiary received Sh200,000 through M-Pesa to help them resettle and rebuild their lives away from the water tower.

Speaking at Sogoo in Narok South Constituency on Wednesday, during the final day of his two-day tour of Narok County, Ruto said the Government had taken steps to address the longstanding Mau Forest resettlement problem.

He noted that in 2023, the Government gave Sh300,000 each to 2,000 families living in tents in the Mau Forest to enable them to leave the water tower and purchase land elsewhere.

“We are today officially closing the long and painful chapter of people who were removed from the Mau Forest, which the County Government of Narok will now manage,” Ruto said.

The President criticised politicians who, he said, had continued to politicise the Mau Forest issue without providing lasting solutions.

“Many politicians have talked of the Mau question, but I talked of the Mau answer. This is why we are here today closing this chapter,” he said.

Ruto also announced that the Government had purchased 5,800 acres of land to settle families who have been living as squatters on property previously owned by the family of former Provincial Commissioner Isaiah Cheluget.

“We are processing title deeds of the people living on the land after buying the Cheluget farm,” he said.

Construction of Johanna Ng'eno University

The President also announced the allocation of Sh1.2 billion for the construction of Johanna Ng’eno University in Emurua Dikirr Constituency.

Speaking during the laying of the foundation stone, Ruto said the institution would fulfil a pledge to residents while expanding access to higher education for students from across the country.

“You told me, as residents of Emurua Dikirr, that you want a university. Today, I have brought KSh1.2 billion to construct the university that will be named after our brother Johana Ng'eno,” he said.

He said the university would create employment opportunities and attract new investments to the region.

At the same time, Ruto maintained that his administration had fulfilled at least 80 per cent of the pledges contained in its 2022 campaign manifesto.

“Kenyans will elect leaders based on their development record. Sloganeering will not make Kenyans vote for them. They have a long way to go,” he said.

The President further launched the construction of the 18-kilometre Mogondo-Cheramgoi-Mogor-Soit road in Emurua Dikirr, saying the project would improve connectivity and unlock economic opportunities in the region.

“This new road will strengthen connectivity and unlock greater economic opportunities in the region,” Ruto said.

World.title: Relief for schools as government releases Sh18.5b capitation
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Education CS Julius Ogamba. [File, Standard]

The government has released Sh18.5 billion in capitation to support operations in public basic education institutions during the third term of 2026, as schools reopened across the country on Monday.

Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba said the funds have already been released and will support learners in pre-primary, primary, junior and senior schools.

The allocation is intended to facilitate smooth school operations and ensure learning activities continue without disruption.

The Sh18.5 billion has been distributed across three major capitation programmes, with Free Day Secondary Education (FDSE) allocated Sh10.963 billion, accounting for the biggest portion of the Term Three capitation.

The money will support operations in public day and secondary schools and comes as institutions prepare learners for a busy academic term.

Free Day Junior School Education has received Sh6.1 billion, to support learners in the second tier of basic education and help institutions meet operational requirements as the Competency-Based Education system continues to expand.

Meanwhile, Free Primary Education has been allocated Sh1.4 billion to support learning in public primary schools.

The funds come as a relief to school heads who had raised concerns on the insufficient funds disbursed to schools this year.

However, Ogamba said the disbursement demonstrates the Government's commitment to ensuring that learners have access to free and compulsory basic education as provided for under Article 53(1)(b) of the Constitution.

“The Government affirms its commitment to fulfil its duty to learners and educational institutions,” said the CS.

Ogamba also warned school heads and principals against misuse of the funds, directing them to ensure the money is spent prudently and for the benefit of learners.

School administrators have further been cautioned against imposing unauthorised levies on parents and learners.

Ogamba said the Ministry would take firm action against institutions found to have misappropriated public resources or imposed illegal charges.

“We will deal firmly with any verified cases of misappropriation of resources and the imposition of unauthorised levies,” he said.

The warning comes as schools reopen for the third term, a period that is expected to be particularly demanding for institutions and learners because of the academic activities and assessments scheduled for the school calendar.

The Ministry has maintained that capitation is meant to ease the financial burden on families and enable schools to provide essential services without passing prohibited costs to parents.

Ogamba reiterated that school administrators must remain accountable for the public funds entrusted to them, warning that verified cases of misuse will attract action from the Ministry.

The Government has also reaffirmed that every child is entitled to free and compulsory basic education, placing the responsibility on education officials and school managers to ensure capitation achieves its intended purpose.

World.title: Ndindi Nyoro begins nationwide political mobilisation ahead of 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro after attending service at Gathuki-ini ACK Church on August 23, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Kiharu MP Ndindi Nyoro has said he will take his campaign for national transformation across Kenya as he positions himself for the 2027 presidential race.

Ndindi said he was interested in leadership committed to addressing concerns in education, health, youth and unemployment, among other needs.

Nyoro, who is the People’s Party of Kenya leader, spoke at St Michael Gathuki-ini ACK Church in Kiharu on Sunday, where he called for respect and political maturity.

Addressing residents in Kiria-ini (Mathioya) and Gakira (Kangema), he urged politicians to engage in a responsible manner.

“I trust in God that after next year Kenya will be able to have leadership that will be responsible for improving citizens' standards of living,” he said.

He regretted that hundreds of university graduates in the area were yet to secure employment.

“I plead with Kenyans to support my course that is geared to transform the nation and ensure equality and transparency,” said the PPK leader.

Nyoro said that after engaging Murang'a residents, he will take his transformation campaigns to all parts of the country.

Speaking at Kiria-ini market, he said he would engage the people to seek their blessings.

“All along had been feeling the urge to lead the country, thus the need to come out in the open and fight for position,” he said.

On Monday, the MP announced his exit from the ruling United Democratic Alliance (UDA), declaring that he will join the opposition ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Nyoro, an economist serving his second term as Kiharu MP, said he will work with opposition leaders to push for what he termed real change in Kenya.

The legislator said all opposition presidential aspirants are welcome at rallies organised by the PPK.

His move marks a significant political shift as parties and leaders begin positioning themselves ahead of the 2027 polls.

World.title: City Hall in rush to expand drainage system ahead of El Nino
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja during an inspection tour of the ongoing drainage system expansion. [GPS]

Nairobi County has embarked on drainage expansion works aimed at mitigating floodwaters ahead of El Nino rains.

Governor Johnson Sakaja, while calling on city residents to remain alert and proactive, said City Hall has intensified preparations and accelerated identification of hotspots.

The governor on Friday said his administration is taking early and coordinated action to minimise the impact of heavy rains, urging residents to stay calm, pay attention to official information and follow guidance from the multi-agency team established to coordinate the city’s preparedness and emergency response.

“We are working proactively to address the challenges of flooding before El Nino hits the ground. We urge our people not to panic but to be alert and get information from our multi-agency team,” said Sakaja.

The Governor spoke during an inspection tour of several flood-prone areas in Nairobi, including the Mombasa Road-Bunyala Junction corridor and Globe Roundabout, which experienced significant flooding during previous heavy rains.

Sakaja said drainage works are already underway in the affected areas, with teams working to open up and deepen drainage channels, clear obstructions, and improve storm-water flow to prevent a repeat of the flooding witnessed previously.

His remarks come as weatherman warned of increased rainfall in the coming months, with Nairobi among the urban areas requiring heightened preparedness because of its exposure to flooding and the impact of heavy rainfall on roads, settlements and other critical infrastructure.

Sakaja said the county has so far brought together the disaster management teams, Kenya Red Cross, Kenya Urban Roads Authority (KURA) and Kenya National Highways Authority (KeNHA) under a coordinated programme worth Sh2.4 billion to strengthen Nairobi’s flood resilience.

Of the amount, Sh2 billion has been set aside for drainage and flood-mitigation works targeting 19 roads in flood-prone areas.

The projects are at an advanced stage, with tenders awarded and contractors expected to commence implementation after completion of the necessary processes.

Sakaja reiterated that the programme will complement ongoing county interventions under the Nairobi Regeneration Programme, which includes the rehabilitation and upgrading of critical infrastructure across the city.

“The Sh2 billion will support a comprehensive drainage overhaul that complements the ongoing Nairobi Regeneration Programme. Our goal is to permanently address the flooding challenges that have affected the city for many years,” Sakaja said.

He said the focus is not only on responding to floods after they occur, but on addressing the infrastructure weaknesses that have historically made Nairobi vulnerable to flooding.

To strengthen preparedness, the county has established five specialised sub-committees under the multi-agency framework.

The committees include Infrastructure and Drainage; Emergency Response and Evacuation; Shelter and Relief; Security and Traffic and Communication.

While the Infrastructure and Drainage committee will coordinate the clearing and improvement of drainage systems, rivers and other critical infrastructure, the Emergency Response and Evacuation committee will oversee rapid response, rescue and evacuation operations whenever emergencies occur.

The Shelter and Relief committee will prepare safe shelters and coordinate the provision of food, water, medical assistance and other essential support to affected residents.

The Security and Traffic committee will coordinate security, traffic management and emergency access, while the Communication committee will strengthen early-warning systems, public alerts and timely dissemination of information.

Sakaja said the county is also mobilising personnel, equipment and other resources to clear blocked drains, remove silt and waste and strengthen emergency response systems in areas identified as vulnerable.

He urged residents and their associations, businesses and other stakeholders to play an active role in flood preparedness by keeping drainage areas clear and paying attention to official warnings.

The county chief said residents in high-risk areas will be provided with timely information on emerging weather conditions and the actions they should take when heavy rains occur.

“We don’t want people to panic. We want people to be proactive, to listen to information and to work with us. The multi-agency team is in place, and we are preparing before the rains intensify,” Sakaja said.

According to him, the multi-agency approach will also help eliminate jurisdictional gaps by bringing together national and county agencies to operate as one coordinated team.

He said the combination of drainage upgrades, emergency preparedness, early-warning systems and coordinated response would strengthen Nairobi’s resilience and reduce disruption caused by heavy rains.

The multi-agency team is expected to meet next week to review progress, coordinate ongoing works and further push the city’s El Niño preparedness agenda.

World.title: Public officers eyeing elective posts to resign by February 10 - IEBC
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon addressing the press at a past press conference. [File, Standard]

Public officers seeking to contest elective positions in the 2027 General Election have until February 10, 2027, to resign from office, the Independent Electoral and Boundaries Commission (IEBC) has announced.

IEBC Chairperson Erastus Ethekon said the deadline falls exactly six months before the August 10, 2027, General Election, which the Commission has confirmed will be held on a Tuesday.

“Any public officer who intends to contest in this election must resign from public office by Wednesday, 10th February 2027, which is exactly six months before the election,” Ethekon said.

The IEBC said adherence to the timelines will be non-negotiable, noting that they are legally binding and essential to ensuring an orderly electoral process.

Under the timetable, political parties must submit their membership lists and details of candidates participating in party primaries by March 16, 2027.

Party primaries and any related disputes must be concluded by May 8, while independent candidates are also required to meet their legal obligations by the same date.

Presidential aspirants will have until May 24 to submit lists of supporting voters drawn from a majority of Kenya’s counties.

Candidate registration will begin on May 29, with specific deadlines applying to the various elective positions.

The official campaign period will commence after candidates are registered, but not earlier than May 29, 2027.

Ethekon warned political parties, candidates and their supporters against breaching the prescribed campaign period, saying any electioneering outside the legal window will be unlawful.

The restrictions cover campaign posters, billboards, political caravans and other forms of campaigning.

Campaigning will close on August 7, 2027, 48 hours before Kenyans head to the polls.

“The law prescribes when election campaigns may commence,” Ethekon said, urging political parties, candidates and their supporters to strictly comply with electoral laws and regulations.

The deadline is among key milestones unveiled by the electoral commission as political parties, aspirants and other stakeholders begin preparations for the next General Election.

World.title: Schools will open on August 24 as scheduled, Ogamba says
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Students heading home during recent demonstrations. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The Ministry of Education said the official academic calendar remains unchanged.

In a statement issued on Wednesday, August 19, Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Ogamba insists that learners will return to school on Monday, August 24, 2026.

The CS has dismissed reports circulating on social media claiming that the reopening of schools for the third term has been postponed, warning parents, teachers, learners and education stakeholders against relying on unauthorised online notices.

“We wish to clarify that the academic calendar for Basic Education institutions and Teacher Training Colleges remains unchanged,” the CS said.

The clarification comes two days before the scheduled reopening of schools, amid reports circulating on social media platforms suggesting that the government had pushed back the start of Term III.

"Our attention has been drawn to misleading information circulating on various social media platforms, purporting that the academic calendar for basic education institutions and Teachers Training Colleges has been changed," he stated.

The Ministry termed the reports “FALSE” and urged members of the public to completely disregard them.

Ogamba said the Ministry had directed Regional Directors of Education, County Directors of Education and Sub-County Directors of Education to ensure strict compliance with the approved academic calendar contained in a circular dated October 9, 2025.

According to the Ministry, pre-primary, primary, junior, senior and secondary schools will begin Term III on Monday, August 24. The term will run for nine weeks and end on October 23, 2026.

The reopening marks the final academic term of the school year, with schools expected to implement the approved programmes as they prepare learners for the end-of-year national assessments and examinations.

Diploma Teachers Training Colleges will also resume academic operations on August 24, with their third term scheduled to conclude on November 6, 2026.

The Ministry further confirmed that the national assessment and examination calendar has not been altered for KPSEA, KILEA, KJSEA, KPLEA and KCSE are scheduled to begin from October 26, 2026, as earlier announced.

The Ministry also reminded schools that extracurricular activities and visits to secondary schools will remain banned during Term III.

The latest clarification is part of efforts by the government to prevent confusion among parents, learners and teachers as schools prepare to reopen.

Ogamba urged education stakeholders to obtain information through official Ministry communication channels, rather than social media posts whose authenticity cannot be established.

“Parents, teachers and learners and members of the public are advised to strictly rely on the Ministry's official communication channels and field officers for accurate information," he said.

World.title: Egypt announce surprise October friendly ahead of AFCON qualifiers
World.content:
The technical staff of the Egyptian national team, led by head coach Hossam Hassan, has scheduled a friendly match against Tanzania on October 5 in Cairo. The fixture forms part of the Pharaohs’ broader preparation strategy for upcoming continental commitments, centered around the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON).

The mid-autumn friendly follows Egypt’s opening fixtures in the qualifying campaign against Angola and South Sudan. Technical staff intend to leverage the international window to assess player fitness, evaluate tactical sharpness, and integrate fringe talent into the squad dynamic ahead of subsequent qualifying rounds, Pulse Mubasher reported.

Egypt’s preparatory camp is scheduled to assemble on September 17 to gear up for the opening double-header. The Pharaohs will host Angola at Cairo International Stadium on September 25 before traveling to Juba to take on South Sudan at Juba National Stadium on September 29. Managing staff view the away fixture in South Sudan as a crucial early test in their push to secure maximum points at the start of the qualifying process.

Following the September fixtures, Egypt will face Malawi in back-to-back qualifying legs in November 2026, before wrapping up their qualifying campaign in March 2027 with return matches against South Sudan and Angola.

World.title: 3 dead, 64 injured in Dabaa bus-truck collision in Matrouh
World.content:
Three people were killed and 64 others injured in a collision between a bus and a trailer truck on the Dabaa Axis road in Matrouh Governorate.

The injured were rushed to El-Dabaa Central Hospital to receive the necessary medical care.

Their injuries varied in severity, including bruises, abrasions, fractures, lacerations, suspected internal bleeding, and miscellaneous trauma, while ongoing medical response and security procedures remain underway regarding the crash.

World.title: Sheikh Zayed kidnapping suspects could face death penalty: Legal expert
World.content:
The suspects involved in the armed kidnapping of a woman in Sheikh Zayed could face the death penalty if convicted, prominent Cassation and Supreme Constitutional Court attorney Amr Abdel Salam stated.

Abdel Salam explained that the legal framework governing the case falls under Article 290 of Egyptian Penal Code No. 58 of 1937, as amended by Law No. 5 of 2018. Under standard provisions, abduction through coercion or fraud carries a minimum rigorous imprisonment sentence of 10 years.

Escalating statutory penalties

The severity of the punishment increases based on specific aggravating circumstances:

Ransom demands: Abductions involving a ransom carry 15 to 20 years of rigorous imprisonment.

Targeting women or minors: If the victim is a woman or a child, the penalty automatically escalates to life imprisonment.

Compounded offenses: Capital punishment (the death penalty) applies if the abduction is linked with sexual assault or rape.

Abdel Salam stressed that final legal classifications and sentencing will depend entirely on the Public Prosecution’s ongoing investigation and evidence gathering.

He also commended law enforcement agencies for apprehending the suspects within 48 hours after video footage documenting the incident surfaced online, highlighting the Interior Ministry’s rapid response in maintaining public safety and deterrence.

World.title: Photos: Manchester City send Egyptian attacker Omar Marmoush to Tottenham on loan
World.content:
Tottenham Hotspur officially announced the signing of Egyptian international forward Omar Marmoush from Manchester City on a season-long loan for the 2026–27 campaign.

The North London club confirmed the transfer via an official statement on Thursday, revealing that the 27-year-old attacker will wear the number 22 shirt during his spell at the club.

Marmoush, who remains under contract with Manchester City through June 2029, originally made the switch to the Etihad Stadium in early 2025 from German outfit Eintracht Frankfurt.

World.title: Trabzonspor head coach resigns following heavy European defeat
World.content:
Fatih Tekke has tendered his resignation as head coach of Trabzonspor in the wake of a devastating 4–0 defeat to Hungarian side Ferencváros. The second-leg loss at the Groupama Aréna sealed a 5–0 aggregate elimination from European competition, prompting the Turkish manager to publicly take full accountability for the collapse.

The aggregate defeat—which ended a campaign featuring Egyptian international Mohamed Salah—proved to be a breaking point. Addressing media directly after the final whistle, Tekke acknowledged the weight of the result during an emotional interview with Turkish broadcaster A Spor, framing the defeat as a deeply painful outcome that left him unable to continue in his position.

Throughout his post-match remarks, Tekke repeatedly shielded his team, pointing to a strict personal philosophy on managerial duty. He insisted that while squad members earn the credit for victories, full responsibility for failure rests squarely on the coaching staff. Although citing unfortunate circumstances and isolated mistakes that spiraled out of control, he conceded that a loss of this magnitude was simply unacceptable.

The resignation comes during a turbulent period for Trabzonspor, marked by mounting media scrutiny and external noise surrounding the club. While recognizing the environment of heightened pressure, Tekke refrained from making excuses, asking supporters for forgiveness as he brought his managerial tenure to a dramatic end.

World.title: Explore the Great Pyramid in VR: Ancient Egypt takes center stage in Buenos Aires
World.content:
History, science, and cutting-edge tech are colliding at La Rural’s Frers Hall. The DG Tech Lab is turning heads in the Argentine capital with five mind-bending Virtual Reality (VR) experiences that blur the line between education and pure entertainment.

Instead of just looking at history through a glass display, visitors can step directly inside it—traveling everywhere from the edge of the cosmos to the inner chambers of the Great Pyramid of Giza.

What’s on the VR menu?

Space explorers: Orbit Earth aboard the International Space Station.

Horizon of Khufu: Stand inside the Great Pyramid of Giza and unlock secrets buried for over 4,500 years.

Secrets of the pyramid builders: Step into the shoes of ancient architects to see how humanity’s greatest wonder was constructed.

The Last fortress: Travel back in time to explore medieval strongholds.

Life Chronicles: Take a thrilling journey across 3.5 billion years of evolution on Earth.

Ancient Egypt takes center stage

Egyptian civilization is a major crowd-puller at the exhibition. Through hyper-realistic graphics, two dedicated VR journeys allow guests to physically walk through Khufu’s grand galleries, giving students and history buffs a rare, hands-on look at ancient engineering and craftsmanship.

By turning immersive VR into an educational tool, the project offers a glimpse into the future of learning—proving that the best way to understand history, science, and the universe is to simply step right inside them.

Main photo source: Horizon of Khufu Official Site.

World.title: EgyptAir becomes exclusive airline partner of FC Barcelona through 2029
World.content:
Egypt’s flag carrier has inked a high-profile sponsorship deal with Spanish football giant FC Barcelona, securing its status as the club’s Official Exclusive Airline Partner through the 2028–2029 season.

Under the multi-year agreement, EgyptAir gains global rights spanning Barcelona’s flagship men’s football team, basketball squad, and handball team. In a notable branding highlight, the airline’s logo will take prime real estate on the front of the handball team’s official match jerseys, alongside a suite of global marketing rights.

Bridging 95 years of aviation with football culture

The partnership marks an ambitious move by EgyptAir to boost its international visibility and appeal to global football fanbases. Capt. Ahmed Adel, Chairman of EgyptAir Holding Company, hailed the deal as an unprecedented milestone that merges the airline’s 95-year aviation legacy with FC Barcelona’s global prestige as reigning La Liga and Spanish Super Cup champions.

EgyptAir Airlines Chairman Capt. Mohamed Elyan emphasized that the collaboration goes beyond routine promotion, framing it as an alignment of shared values—excellence, commitment, and teamwork—designed to strengthen EgyptAir’s position in competitive global aviation markets.

Barcelona officials mirrored the enthusiasm, with Marc Broix, Global Sponsorship Director at FC Barcelona, noting that aligning with Egypt’s flagship carrier represents a natural step in the Catalan club’s ongoing international expansion.

World.title: No Salmonella outbreak in Egypt, Health Ministry confirms
World.content:
Minister of Health Dr. Khaled Abdel Ghaffar confirmed that the ministry is actively monitoring local and international health conditions through event-based epidemiological surveillance systems targeting foodborne illnesses, particularly Salmonella.

Following reported outbreaks in several countries tied to international supply chains, the ministry is conducting continuous risk assessments and rapid evaluations to prepare precautionary measures if needed.

Local status vs. international outbreaks

Dr. Abdel Ghaffar emphasized that monitoring global health events does not indicate a current risk within Egypt, but rather serves as a proactive early warning measure. Decision-making relies strictly on domestic data, surveillance metrics, and verified global reports rather than external cases alone.

No unusual outbreaks detected nationally

Dr. Amr Kandil, Deputy Minister of Health, noted that the Preventive Medicine and Public Health sector tracks daily changes in infection patterns and assesses reports based on established scientific standards. He confirmed that no unusual Salmonella outbreaks connected to recent international events have been recorded in Egypt.

Global case tracking: Belgium and the United Kingdom

Ministry Spokesperson Dr. Hossam Abdel Ghaffar detailed specific international incidents currently under review:

Belgium: Over 306 cases of Salmonella Enteritidis (updated August 25) with zero deaths, resulting in product recalls across Belgium and Luxembourg.

United Kingdom: The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) reported 207 confirmed cases of Salmonella Enteritidis and one death as of August 18.

Response protocols and public safety guidelines

Dr. Radhy Hammad, Head of the Preventive Medicine and Public Health Sector, stated that countering foodborne pathogens relies on swift case identification, epidemiological investigation, supply tracing, and containment.

The Ministry of Health advises the public to adhere to essential food safety practices:

Wash hands thoroughly with soap and water before handling food and after using the restroom.

Separate raw and cooked foods using designated utensils and surfaces.

Cook food thoroughly to safe internal temperatures.

Store perishable foods at proper refrigerated temperatures.

Purchase food items exclusively from trusted sources and follow official recall advisories.

The ministry reaffirmed that its epidemiological surveillance infrastructure remains proactive and operational to safeguard public health.

World.title: Liberia: Supreme Court Denies Koffa, Co-Defendants’ Prohibition Petition, Clears Way for Capitol Arson Trial
World.content:
High Court Upholds Judge Willie’s Authority to Disband Jury; Koffa Team’s Challenge Rejected

By:Willie N. Tokpah

Monrovia-The Supreme Court of Liberia has denied a petition for a Writ of Prohibition filed by former House Speaker J. Fonati Koffa and several co-defendants in the Capitol Building arson case, clearing the way for Criminal Court “A” to proceed with the prosecution.

The ruling represents a major victory for the prosecution and effectively rejects the defendants’ attempt to overturn Resident Judge Roosevelt Z. Willie’s decision to disband the jury previously empaneled to hear the case.

The petitioners, including Koffa, Dixon W. Seboe, Abu B. Kamara, K. Jacob C. B. Debee, Christian Kofa, John Nyanti, Eric Susay, Thomas Isaac Etheridge and Stephen Broh, had asked the Supreme Court to restrain Judge Willie from proceeding after he dissolved the jury following allegations of juror misconduct.

The Supreme Court, however, found no sufficient legal basis to issue the extraordinary writ, holding that Judge Willie acted within his lawful authority in making the decision concerning the jury.

The decision does not determine the guilt or innocence of Koffa and his co-defendants.

Rather, it resolves the immediate legal challenge over whether the trial judge acted unlawfully in disbanding the jury.

Why Judge Willie Disbanded The Jury

The controversy arose after prosecutors asked the trial court to dissolve the entire jury, alleging that the panel had become compromised and could no longer fairly and independently adjudicate the case.

The prosecution pointed to several incidents involving jurors during testimony, including questions raised concerning evidence presented by the State.

One of the disputed incidents occurred during the testimony of LNP Chief Superintendent Rafael A. Wilson.

A juror questioned Wilson after he testified concerning photographs and evidence gathered during the investigation of the Capitol Building fire.

According to the proceedings, the juror questioned how photographs had been obtained when Wilson had earlier indicated that there was no CCTV camera inside the Capitol Building.

The juror subsequently asked that a photograph be produced and, after it was exhibited, raised a question concerning whether a person appearing in the image resembled defendant Thomas Isaac Etheridge.

Prosecutors argued that the nature of the questioning suggested that the juror had already begun evaluating the evidence and forming an opinion about a defendant before the conclusion of the trial.

The State further alleged that some jurors had consulted among themselves before putting questions to witnesses, which prosecutors argued demonstrated a loss of impartiality and undermined their ability to fairly determine the case.

Defense Rejected Claims Of Juror Misconduct

Koffa and his co-defendants strongly challenged the prosecution’s allegations.

Their legal team argued that prosecutors had failed to identify specific jurors who had committed misconduct and had, in some instances, mischaracterized or misquoted the jurors’ remarks.

The defense maintained that jurors asking questions about evidence did not, by itself, constitute misconduct.

They further argued that even if misconduct had been committed by an individual juror, such conduct could not automatically be attributed to the entire panel.

According to the defense, there was no sufficient evidence that the jurors had received outside influence, improperly communicated with outsiders or reached conclusions concerning the defendants’ guilt before deliberations.

The defense therefore argued that there was no legal basis to dissolve the entire jury or declare a mistrial.

Political Affiliation Also Became An Issue

The jury controversy was further complicated by the removal of one juror after the court determined that she had failed to disclose during jury selection that she held a leadership position within the Congress for Democratic Change

The prosecution raised concerns about potential bias because some of the defendants have political associations with the CDC.

Another juror was challenged after prosecutors presented photographs they claimed showed her among supporters at an event associated with defendant Abu B. Kamara.

Judge Willie, however, rejected that challenge after finding that the photographs had not been sufficiently authenticated to establish that the person depicted was the juror.

The juror denied that she was the woman in the photograph and maintained that the person shown was her mother.

Supreme Court Says, Prohibition Cannot Lie

The defendants subsequently turned to the Supreme Court, arguing that Judge Willie’s decision to disband the jury was unlawful.

The High Court had previously intervened in the matter, including ordering a stay of proceedings while the prohibition petition was considered.

But after scrutinizing the arguments, the Supreme Court has now declined to grant the requested relief.

The Court essentially determined that the trial judge had acted within the authority vested in him to make the disputed ruling concerning the jury.

The petition for prohibition was therefore denied.

The case stems from the December 18, 2024 fire at Liberia’s Capitol Building, an incident that damaged portions of the country’s legislative complex and triggered a major criminal investigation.

The government subsequently charged Koffa and several others in connection with an alleged conspiracy surrounding the fire.

The defendants have pleaded not guilty to all charges and have consistently challenged the prosecution’s allegations and evidence.

The proceedings have involved contentious disputes over witness testimony, photographs, videos, audio recordings and other evidence the prosecution intends to use to establish its case.

The jury controversy became one of the most consequential procedural battles in the trial after prosecutors argued that questions raised by jurors demonstrated that the panel had become compromised.

Judge Willie ultimately sided with the prosecution and disbanded the jury.

Koffa and his co-defendants then sought Supreme Court intervention.

World.title: Liberia: Fundamental Weaknesses In State’s Evidence Against Murder Suspect Kaiser
World.content:
Supreme Court Overturns Lower Court’s Conviction, Orders His Release, After Years In Prison

‘State’s Evidence Failed to Corroborate’, As High Court Restores Rights of Man Convicted in Fatu Blasuah Murder

By Willie N. Tokpah

Monrovia- The murder conviction of Valington B. Kaiser, alias “Bishop,” has been overturned by the Supreme Court of Liberia, declaring that the evidence presented by the prosecution failed to sufficiently corroborate the case against him and ordering that his rights and dignity be restored.

Kaiser, who has spent more than three years behind bars at the Monrovia Central Prison, walked away from the country’s highest court a free man Friday, following the landmark decision.

The ruling brings a dramatic turn to a murder case that began with the brutal killing of 18-year-old Fatu Blasuah at the former LPRC compound in Monrovia in May 2022 and culminated in Kaiser’s conviction before Criminal Court “A” in March 2023.

The Supreme Court, in reviewing the lower court’s judgment, found fundamental weaknesses in the State’s evidentiary case, concluding that the pieces of evidence relied upon by the prosecution did not sufficiently corroborate one another to sustain Kaiser’s conviction.

With the conviction overturned, the Supreme Court has restored Kaiser’s legal standing and liberty, bringing an end, at least for now, to more than three years of incarceration stemming from a conviction the nation’s highest court has now rejected.

From Murder Scene To Prison Cell

The case dates back to May 16, 2022, when the body of Fatu Blasuah was discovered at the Old LPRC Compound in Monrovia.

Police reported that the 18-year-old had suffered multiple stab wounds.

Investigators reportedly recovered a silver knife with a green handle from the scene.

Kaiser, who was then about 20 years old, was subsequently arrested and accused of involvement in the killing.

Investigators also pointed to CCTV footage which they said placed Kaiser in or around the area where Fatu’s body was discovered.

The prosecution further alleged that Kaiser and Fatu had been involved in a romantic relationship before her death.

Those allegations formed part of the evidence presented against him at trial.

A Mother’s Testimony

During the trial, Fatu’s mother, Maima Sackie, testified about her daughter’s relationship with Kaiser and the events preceding her disappearance.

She told the court that Kaiser was known to the family and frequently visited Fatu.

According to her testimony, Fatu left home after telling her that Kaiser had contacted her concerning a phone he had left with her.

Fatu did not return home that evening.

The family later became alarmed and eventually learned that a body had been discovered around the LPRC area.

The prosecution relied on the testimony, along with the CCTV footage, the knife reportedly recovered from the scene and other evidence, to build its case against Kaiser.

Jury Found Kaiser Guilty

After approximately a month-long trial before Criminal Court “A,” a 12-member jury returned a guilty verdict against Kaiser on March 1, 2023.

Reports from the time indicated that 10 of the 12 jurors voted to convict him.

The verdict resulted in Kaiser’s continued detention at the Monrovia Central Prison, where he remained for years while pursuing legal remedies against his conviction.

But the case did not end with the jury’s verdict.

Kaiser challenged the judgment, eventually bringing the matter before the Supreme Court—the final judicial authority in Liberia.

Evidence Did Not Corroborate

In its review, the Supreme Court scrutinized the evidence upon which the conviction rested.

The High Court determined that the various pieces of evidence presented by the State failed to adequately corroborate one another, raising serious questions about whether the prosecution had met the legal threshold required to sustain a criminal conviction.

The significance of the ruling is profound.

A guilty verdict by a trial jury cannot stand simply because suspicion surrounds an accused person.

The prosecution must establish guilt through legally sufficient evidence.

In Kaiser’s case, the Supreme Court has now determined that the evidentiary pieces relied upon by the State were insufficiently corroborated to sustain the judgment against him.

From Convicted Murderer To Free Man

The decision dramatically changes Kaiser’s legal status.

For more than three years, he lived behind the walls of the Monrovia Central Prison after being convicted of one of the most serious crimes under Liberian law.

On Friday, August 28, that conviction was overturned by the Supreme Court.

The ruling restores his liberty and, with it, the presumption of innocence that stands at the heart of Liberia’s criminal justice system.

Kaiser is now a free man.

World.title: Liberia: Maryland County Senator Engages Liberian Embassy, Diaspora Leaders in France
World.content:
Amb. Teeko Tozay Yorlay, Sr. (left) and Senator James Biney of

Maryland County.

PARIS, France – A Maryland County Senator, who chairs the Liberian Senate Committee on Executive and serves as ranking member of the Committee on Foreign Affairs, has held separate engagements with officials at the Liberian Embassy in Paris and leaders of the Liberian community in France.

By Jaheim T. Tumu

According to a release, the Senator visited the Embassy of Liberia in Paris on Thursday, where he was received by Liberia’s Ambassador to France, Dr. Teeko Tozay Yorlay, Sr., and members of the diplomatic staff.

During the meeting, the Senator commended Ambassador Yorlay and the Embassy staff for their service to Liberia, particularly the sacrifices and challenges associated with representing the country abroad.

He praised the mission’s dedication, resilience and commitment to duty, noting that Liberia’s diplomatic representatives play an important role in advancing the country’s foreign-policy interests, providing services to Liberians abroad and strengthening relations with France and other countries of accreditation.

The Senator encouraged the Embassy staff to remain committed to their national responsibilities and continue upholding Liberia’s interests in their diplomatic engagements.

Senator Meets Liberian Community Leaders

Following his engagement at the Embassy, the Senator met with the leadership of the Federation of Liberian Associations in France as part of his outreach to Liberians living in France and across Europe.

The meeting provided an opportunity for the Federation’s leadership to present its vision, priorities and ongoing efforts to promote unity, cooperation and community development among Liberians in France.

The group also briefed the Senator on preparations for the upcoming Liberian Independence Day celebrations in Europe under the European Federation of Liberian Associations (EFLA).

The Federation described the annual gathering as an important platform for promoting Liberian culture, national identity, diaspora solidarity and stronger connections between Liberians abroad and their homeland.

Discussions also focused on the need for greater and sustained engagement between the Government of Liberia and diaspora organizations across Europe.

The Federation highlighted the potential contribution of the Liberian diaspora to national development through investment, knowledge and skills transfer, advocacy, tourism promotion and other forms of constructive engagement.

Call for Stronger Government-Diaspora Engagement

The Senator welcomed the concerns and recommendations presented by the Federation and acknowledged the significant contributions Liberians abroad continue to make to the country’s development.

He emphasized the importance of maintaining effective channels of communication between the Government of Liberia and organized diaspora communities, particularly those in Europe.

The Senator encouraged the Federation to continue working collaboratively to promote the interests and welfare of Liberians in France while contributing to Liberia’s broader national development agenda.

The engagements in Paris concluded with a shared commitment to strengthening Liberia’s diplomatic service, deepening Government-diaspora relations and ensuring that the concerns, aspirations and contributions of Liberians living in Europe remain an important part of national development discussions.

World.title: Liberia: Finance Unlocks Jobs, Hope”-Governor Saamoi Declares as CBL Launches Enhanced Collateral Registry Aimed at Boosting Secured Lending
World.content:
As CBL Launches Enhanced Collateral Registry Aimed at Boosting Secured Lending

Congo Town– The Central Bank of Liberia (CBL) has launched an Enhanced Collateral Registry System, a major financial sector reform aimed at expanding access to credit for businesses and individuals by allowing lenders and borrowers to more efficiently register and verify collateral through a modern digital platform.

By Jaheim T. [email protected]

The launch, attended by senior government officials, development partners, representatives of financial institutions, and members of the private sector, marked what CBL Executive Governor Henry F. Saamoi described as an important step toward strengthening secured lending, promoting responsible borrowing, and deepening financial inclusion across Liberia.

In his keynote address, Governor Saamoi said the new system is designed to help unlock financing opportunities for entrepreneurs, small businesses, farmers, and other productive sectors of the economy that often struggle to access formal credit despite owning valuable assets.

“We are not merely launching a technological platform. We are launching a powerful instrument for economic empowerment,” Saamoi said.

“We are launching a reform that will help unlock capital, expand opportunity, and strengthen the foundations of inclusive economic growth in Liberia.”

The Governor explained that many Liberian businesses possess assets such as equipment, contracts, vehicles, inventory, and land, but have historically faced challenges converting those assets into bankable collateral due to weaknesses in the country’s credit infrastructure.

According to him, the enhanced registry addresses that challenge by creating a more transparent, reliable, and accessible framework for secured transactions.

The modernized system allows both movable and immovable assets to be registered through a unified digital platform that can be accessed around the clock.

Financial institutions can electronically register, amend, assign, discharge, and search security interests more efficiently, reducing delays and uncertainty in lending transactions.

Saamoi said the initiative forms part of Liberia’s broader effort to build a modern financial system capable of supporting investment, job creation, and sustainable economic growth.

He noted that the reform is aligned with the government of Liberia’s ARREST Agenda for Inclusive Development, which emphasizes inclusive economic growth and expanded access to financial services.

“We are not simply introducing new technology,” the Governor said. “The Enhanced Collateral Registry represents another important milestone in our collective efforts to modernize Liberia’s financial infrastructure and create a financial system that works for every Liberian.”

One of the key features of the upgraded platform is its ability to connect with other national databases and institutions.

The registry is linked with institutions such as the National Identification Registry, the Liberia Land Authority, the Liberia Business Registry, and vehicle registration systems.

This interoperability enables lenders to verify ownership information, identity records, and existing claims on assets with greater confidence.

According to the Saamoi, better access to reliable information will help reduce lending risks, strengthen transparency, and improve confidence within the financial system.

Experts say these improvements could encourage financial institutions to expand lending to sectors that have traditionally been underserved.

Saamoi emphasized that the reform could have a particularly strong impact on micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs), which remain the backbone of Liberia’s economy.

He said many entrepreneurs possess productive assets but are unable to access financing because traditional lending models often favor conventional forms of collateral.

“For too long, many small businesses, women-owned enterprises, young entrepreneurs, farmers, and rural producers have lacked access to traditional financing despite owning productive assets,” he said.

“A more inclusive financial system is not merely a banking objective. It is a national development imperative.”

Governor Saamoi said the true success of the registry would not be measured by the technology itself but by its impact on people’s lives and businesses.

“The real value of this platform will not be measured by the technology itself,” he said. “Its true value will be measured by the businesses it helps grow, the investments it supports, the jobs it creates, and the lives it transforms.”

The Governor summarized the broader vision behind the reform. “Today, we launch an enhanced system. Tomorrow, we unlock finance. Finance unlocks enterprise. Enterprise unlocks jobs. And jobs unlock hope.”

During his remarks, the Governor pointed to results achieved under the Liberia Investment, Finance and Trade (LIFT) Project as evidence that increased access to finance can produce positive economic outcomes.

He disclosed that a US$6 million line of credit established under the project had been fully deployed through seven participating financial institutions by the second quarter of 2026.

According to the Central Bank, the facility helped 358 MSMEs obtain affordable financing, with some businesses receiving loans of up to US$100,000.

The Governor further revealed that women-owned businesses accounted for 64 percent of all loan disbursements, while 130 beneficiary enterprises were located outside Montserrado County.

Reflecting on those achievements, Saamoi said the data demonstrates that Liberian entrepreneurs have the capacity to grow if given adequate support and access to financing.

“The truth is that Liberian entrepreneurs do not lack ambition. Liberian entrepreneurs do not lack innovation. Liberian entrepreneurs do not lack determination,” he said. “Too often, they simply lack access.”

Development partners also welcomed the launch and described it as an important milestone in Liberia’s economic development agenda.

World Bank Country Manager, Georgia Wallen said access to finance remains one of the biggest obstacles facing Liberian businesses.

She noted that many entrepreneurs possess productive assets but lack the traditional collateral required by lenders to secure financing.

“The Enhanced Collateral Registry System helps to bridge this gap,” Wallen said. “It will give lenders greater confidence to accept a wider range of assets, and it will help borrowers unlock the value of the assets that they possess.”

She recalled that Liberia’s first collateral registry, launched in 2014 with support from the International Finance Corporation (IFC), had produced encouraging results by facilitating more than US$237 million in financing within its first two years of operation.

According to Wallen, the enhanced version seeks to build upon those gains while addressing challenges identified over time.

Wallen stressed, however, that technology alone would not guarantee success. She said widespread adoption by banks, businesses, regulators, and other stakeholders would be necessary to ensure the registry achieves its intended objectives. She disclosed that training programs and public awareness campaigns are already being planned to support implementation.

The judiciary also expressed strong support for the reform. Commercial Court Judge Eva Mappy Morgan described the enhanced registry as a critical development that could improve transparency in lending transactions and strengthen the enforcement of financial agreements.

Morgan explained that disputes often arise when collateral cannot be properly identified or when multiple claims exist over the same asset.

She said the new system would help provide clarity regarding ownership and security interests, reducing legal uncertainties that have historically complicated the recovery of non-performing loans.

A more reliable collateral framework, she added, could increase confidence among lenders and investors while strengthening the overall business environment.

As Liberia continues its broader financial sector modernization agenda, the Central Bank says the Enhanced Collateral Registry will work alongside a modernized Credit Reference System currently being developed under the LIFT Project. Both systems are expected to improve credit information, support better lending decisions, and strengthen confidence throughout the financial sector.

World.title: Liberia: Supreme Court Recalls US$50,000 Fines Against Martin Kollie, Alex Williams
World.content:
MONROVIA — The Supreme Court of Liberia has recalled and corrected a portion of its ruling delivered Thursday, August 27, in a damages case involving former LISGIS Deputy Director General Wilmot Smith and Ecobank Liberia.

By: Willie N. Tokpah

Chief Justice Yamie Quiqui Gbeisay, as the Court resumed its ongoing ruling session on Friday, August 28, clarified that the inclusion of activist Martin K.N. Kollie and Alex Williams in a US$50,000 general damages award each was an inadvertent error in the Full Bench’s opinion.

According to the Court’s clarification, Kollie and Williams were not parties to the case before the lower court in the manner contemplated by the judgment and, therefore, could not properly be subjected to the damages award.

The Supreme Court consequently cancelled the US$50,000 award against Kollie and the separate US$50,000 award against Williams.

However, the Court’s US$250,000 special damages award against Ecobank Liberia remains in effect.

The clarification came just one day after Thursday’s ruling generated widespread public attention, particularly over the inclusion of Kollie and Williams in the damages portion of the judgment.

With Friday’s correction, Ecobank Liberia remains solely responsible for the US$250,000 award arising from the Supreme Court’s decision in the matter involving Smith.

Following Thursday’s ruling, Kollie and Williams separately took to Facebook to challenge the decision, saying they had never been cited or informed about any case involving them.

Both said the inclusion of their names in the judgment came as a surprise.

The Supreme Court’s clarification now removes the financial penalties against the two men, while leaving the US$250,000 special damages award against Ecobank Liberia intact.

More details are expected as the Supreme Court continues its ongoing ruling session.

Summary

Tuesday’s preliminary hearing in the cocaine trafficking case against former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor has been pushed to Wednesday, September 2, at 10:00 a.m., after the Ministry of Justice requested a last-minute continuance. The delay comes as questions grow around the state’s timeline linking her to an alleged cocaine network.

Court Grants Continuance Hours Before First Hearing Was Set to Open

By Rodney D. Sieh, [email protected]

MONROVIA — The preliminary hearing in the cocaine trafficking case against former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor will not go forward until next as Wednesday, September 2, 2026.

Early this morning, The Ministry of Justice’s Office of the City Solicitor asked the Monrovia City Court for a continuance just hours before the case was due to open, and Stipendiary Magistrate Cllr. L. Ben Barco granted it.

The hearing will now resume Wednesday, September 2, at 10:00 a.m.

In its request, the government said the Supreme Court’s closing of its March Term of Court had pulled several senior lawyers away to attend on their supervisors, leaving the prosecution short of the counsel it needed for the day.

It is a short delay, but it lands at a moment when the state’s own account of the case is drawing closer scrutiny. Howard-Taylor faces nine charges built around allegations that a businessman, Sheikh Bassirou Kante, introduced her to an alleged Croatian-Ukrainian cocaine network in “early 2022,” first at her Congo Town residence and later in Dubai.

What has quietly complicated that narrative is a matter of public U.S. court record: Kante was arrested in Maryland on April 20, 2022, on wire fraud and money laundering charges unrelated to narcotics.

The charge sheet gives no specific date for the Congo Town meeting or the Dubai trip, and no travel records placing Kante in Liberia or the Gulf ahead of his arrest have yet been made public. That gap has left room for a question the defense is expected to press hard on Wednesday: where, precisely, was everyone when this was supposed to have happened?

Howard-Taylor has denied all charges.

Her legal team has called the case baseless and politically motivated and says it will contest it vigorously when the hearing resumes.

FrontPageAfrica will continue to follow this story as it develops.

World.title: UTH Paediatric surgeons conduct 30 operations in Kasama
World.content:
A team of Paediatric surgeons from the University Teaching Hospital(UTH) has successfully performed 30 operations during a four-day surgical camp at Kasama General Hospital.

UTH Paediatric Surgeon Amon Ngongola, who is leading the team, disclosed that seven of the procedures were major surgeries involving children with complex medical conditions.

Dr Ngongola said the team performed several anoplasty procedures on babies born without a normal anal opening, reconstructing the affected area to enable them to pass stool normally.

He expressed gratitude with the positive response from the community in Northern Province and beyond.

“We had patients coming all the way from Mpulungu and Nakonde Districts,” Dr Ngogola said.

He commended the medical team at Kasama General Hospital for its work ethic and efficiency.

And Kasama General Hospital, General Surgeon Bright Nseluka, said the surgical camp has significantly helped reduce the health facility’s referral costs.

Dr Nseluka added that the hospital has also benefited from the knowledge and skills transfer from the team of specialists.

Meanwhile, parents whose children underwent successful surgeries have hailed the exercise describing it as life-saving.

One of the parents, Cecilia Kasonde, whose child was born without a normal anal opening, expressed happiness that her child’s situation was normalised.

World.title: ZTA urges private sector participation to increase tourist arrivals
World.content:
Zambia Tourism Agency (ZTA), says stronger collaboration, reliable tourism data and active private sector participation are critical to achieving Government’s target of attracting at least five million international tourist arrivals by 2031.

ZTA Acting Chief Executive Officer, Abigail Shansonga, says the tourism sector cannot be driven by one institution alone, but requires coordinated efforts from Government, the private sector, communities and other stakeholders.

Ms Shansonga said this in Lusaka today during the Ministry of Tourism stakeholder engagement meeting to review sector performance and gather input into the 2027 destination marketing programme.

She said reliable tourism data is particularly important for planning, market selection, investment decisions and measuring the impact of tourism across the country.

“Better data is not merely a reporting obligation, it is a competitive asset for the whole destination,” Ms Shansonga said.

Ms Shansonga also called on tourism businesses to actively participate in ZTA marketing initiatives by providing current product information, creating bookable packages, following up trade leads and sharing market intelligence.

And ZTA Board Chairperson, Keira Johnson said achieving the five million arrival target will require competitive tourism products, reliable air access, high service standards and sustained public-private collaboration.

“We have one agenda today, to grow Zambian tourism sustainably. Not one agenda for government and one for the private sector. Not one agenda for ZTA and one for the tourism associations. One agenda, one destination, one industry, one Zambia,” Mrs Johnson said.

And Tourism Council of Zambia Chairperson, Glyden Mungaila commended Government and the Zambia Tourism Agency for strengthening engagement with the industry, saying partnerships are essential to positioning destination Zambia on the global tourism market.

Ms Mungaila said the tourism industry has recorded increased growth, energy and cohesion in recent years, while calling for broader representation of different tourism products and destinations in the 2027 strategy.

“We stand here today as co-partners in the marketing and positioning of Destination Zambia, united by shared ambition and shared responsibility in taking Zambia to the World,” she said.

Meanwhile, Board of Airlines Representatives Zambia Board Secretary, Hellen Mwansa identified high operating costs and taxes, air connectivity and market development, and regulatory and operational efficiency as three priority areas requiring attention.

Ms Mwansa said improving these areas would create a more competitive operating environment for airlines and support the growth of tourism, noting that stronger air connectivity is essential to expanding Zambia’s international visitor markets.

“The three areas to reiterate that we believe require attention are high operational cost, stronger air connectivity and market development, and more efficient and predictable regulatory and operational processes,” Ms Mwansa said.
